jobs.title: Chief Development Officer, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
"the Great Educational Equalizer"

— Philosopher Johnathan Bi, on Alpha School

Alpha is hiring.

You went into private school leadership to shape how children learn, not to run capital campaigns and referee parent committees. There is a version of this job where the academic model is protected for you, operations is handled centrally, and you spend your week on what you are best at: winning over the families who matter most, turning them into advocates, and being the voice of authority when the conversation gets hard.

You will own the parent side of Alpha in one metro — Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles. Your measure is enrollment and advocacy: prospective ultra-high-net-worth families who convert, current UHNW families who re-enroll, refer, and publicly champion 2 Hour Learning, and a local community where Alpha is top of mind. Roughly half your week is outward-facing — community partnerships, info sessions, and 1:1 conversations with sophisticated parents who have read every AI skeptic and want to know why the model actually works.

The rest of the seat is the escalation line. When an Associate Dean of Parents reaches the edge of what they can resolve — a board family threatening to pull their kids, a campus quietly softening the model to keep a vocal parent happy — it comes to you. You retain the family, and you keep the model intact. Both. Then you document the precedent so the Associate Dean network can handle it next time without you.

If you have run a private or independent K-12 school, or you have spent a career earning the trust of UHNW families in another industry, and you have been waiting for the job where judgment and persuasion are the actual deliverables, this is it.

What You Will Be Doing

Building local awareness through partnerships with family offices, private clubs, and independent advisors, plus workshops and community events that generate inbound interest
Running admissions for wealthy families end to end: info sessions, 1:1 follow-up in the CRM, and the enrollment decision, including telling a family this is not the right school for their child
Turning enrolled parents into public champions of 2 Hour Learning through advocacy workshops and parent-to-parent networks, so enrolled families become your strongest source of new inquiries
Resolving the escalations others cannot: diagnosing whether the problem is the model, campus execution, or family fit, engaging the family directly, then writing up the precedent for the rest of the network
Keeping current families close through regular touchpoints, and reporting the patterns you hear back to leadership

What You Won’t Be Doing

Capital campaigns, donor cultivation, major gifts, and every other form of fundraising are off your plate entirely
Convening PTAs, School Improvement Councils, parent committees, or focus groups that get a vote on school policy
Managing facilities, finance, legal, vendors, technology, marketing, or community logistics — centralized teams own all of this, so your week stays on relationships, not operations
Designing curriculum or coaching instructional staff on pedagogy; the academic model is owned and protected centrally
Making exceptions or customizations to the educational model to satisfy a parent request, however influential the parent
Simply logging and responding to complaints, or writing newsletters and routine parent communications
Defusing conflict by avoiding it — diplomacy here means delivering hard messages, not softening standards
Working behind the scenes; this is an on-site, full-time, face-of-the-school seat that includes evening and weekend community events

Chief Development Officer Key Responsibilities

Build a metro where Alpha families are 2 Hour Learning’s loudest advocates — and where no parent crisis is resolved by compromising the model.

Basic Requirements

7+ years leading high-stakes relationships in private or independent K-12 education, fundraising or major gifts, enterprise sales, client success, or private wealth management
2+ years working directly and regularly with ultra-high-net-worth or similarly high-expectation families, such as full-pay families at an elite private school, family-office clients, wealth-management clients, or major donors
Proven ownership of measurable enrollment, retention, advocacy, sales, or client outcomes, including resolving sensitive situations and holding firm standards when influential people push back
Polished executive communication, consultative judgment, and genuine conviction in Alpha's accelerated learning model, with the confidence to represent it to skeptical parents and public stakeholders
Living in the Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles metro area; authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship; and available for full-time on-site work, including 2 to 4 evening or weekend events per month

Nice-to-have Requirements

Sitting or recent Head of School — or the Head’s right hand — at a top-tier independent K-12 (NAIS-member or peer tier)
Multi-campus or multi-site school leadership experience (regional director, network superintendent, COO of a school network)
A UHNW client-services background translated into school leadership: private wealth management, single-family office, or major-gifts development at an elite prep or Ivy
An existing network among UHNW families or influential local organizations in Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles
Crisis communication experience involving press, regulators, or board-level stakeholders
Hands-on AI building experience — custom GPTs, agents, or vibe-coded internal tools used in a real operating context
An advanced degree (M.Ed., MBA, or doctorate) — common in this profile, but not required; no formal education is required for this role

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time, W2 employee position with immediate access to benefits (https://support.crossover.com/article/7581-w2-benefits-u-s-paychex-paid-only). All roles are year-long positions. The compensation level for this role is $400,000 USD/year. The payment period is weekly. Consult www.crossover.com/help-and-faqs for more details on this topic.

jobs.title: Program Director, Center of Innovation
jobs.description:
Who We Are

We are Tennis! The USTA (United States Tennis Association) is the national governing body for the sport of tennis and the leader in promoting and developing the sport’s growth on every level in the United States, from local communities to the crown jewel of the professional game, the US Open.

The USTA Foundation Incorporated (USTAF or USTA Foundation) is the social impact arm of the United States Tennis Association Incorporated (USTA), utilizing the powerful combination of tennis and education to enhance the lives of under-resourced youth through its support of the National Junior Tennis & Learning (NJTL) network. For more than 50 years, NJTL has impacted thousands of under-resourced youth across the nation, and today the network features more than 270 chapters that reach more than 233,000,000 young people from under-resourced communities annually.

Why Work for the USTA?

We are a passionate team of staff and volunteers focused on growing the sport of tennis and making it accessible to all. We are committed to removing barriers and creating opportunities for ALL to participate.

About Lulu's Place

Lulu's Place will offer state-of-the-art facilities in Los Angeles, north of LAX airport, between the communities of Westchester and Playa del Rey, bringing together academic, athletic, and wellness programs for youth from all backgrounds. Trusted partners, including TGR Foundation, a Tiger Woods charity; the United States Tennis Association (USTA) and its charitable arm, USTA Foundation; Cedars-Sinai; and Providence will bring together professional teachers, coaches, mentors, and service providers to deliver high-quality programs to children and their families.

The vision for this project is rooted in the passion and generosity of Carol "Lulu" Kimmelman, a Southern California native, former elementary school teacher in South Los Angeles, and lifelong tennis player who passed away in 2017 after a courageous battle with ovarian cancer. Today, her husband, Doug Kimmelman, and their four children honor Lulu's legacy by advancing her mission to transform young people's lives and create greater equity in sports and education through this groundbreaking youth center.

The Role

The Program Director at Lulu’s Place will lead a youth development program focused on college and career readiness and non-degree career pathways, operating within a shared facility alongside several partner organizations. This position involves a managerial component, overseeing program staff and volunteers.

Operational Oversight: Manage day-to-day operations for USTAF Center of Innovation (CoI), ensuring all activities align with the foundation’s mission, goals, priorities, and safety standards.
Partner Integration: Lead coordination efforts with Lulu's Place Leadership, TGR Foundation, and other on-site program partners to successfully align on shared goals and execution of educational and tennis programming.
Program Development: Lead design and oversee the planning and implementation for direct day, weekend, and afterschool programming. The programs will incorporate the core principles of the NJTL network, tennis, education, and mentorship
Community Engagement: Sets the strategy and is responsible for the USTAF CoI engagement with local community partners, including greater LA NJTL organizations, school districts, charter schools, youth development organizations, and other key community stakeholders.
Quality Assurance: Responsible for the oversight and delivery of USTAF programs and partnered programs to accomplish established and shared goals.
Strategic Growth: Identify opportunities to test and expand programs/products to increase the reach and enhance the impact of NJTL sports-based interventions within the community.

Partner & Facility Coordination

Stakeholder Liaison: Serve as the primary point of contact for diverse community partners, including non-profits, schools, and local NJTL organizations.
Facility Scheduling: Work with the Lulu’s Place facility team and partners to manage the complex master calendars for shared facility use, balancing USTAF programming needs with Lulu's Place partners and community access.
Collaborative Governance: Represent the USTAF by attending all regular partner meetings to ensure effective, efficient communication, align priorities, and minimize confusion and conflicts.
Resource Allocation: Responsible for the USTAF offices and footprint at Lulu's Place.

Impact Measurement & Reporting

Data Collection: Implement systems to track participant attendance, demographic data, and youth development outcomes across all partner programs.
Align with the USTAF leadership in the development of the “measures of success” and align with Lulu's Place partners to align on shared goals

Reporting: Capture and deliver program data into reports for foundation leadership, donors, and community stakeholders.
Evaluation: Use qualitative and quantitative feedback to assess the effectiveness of the "collective impact" model at the facility site.

Compliance & Administration

Safety & Risk Management: Ensure all partners and staff meet Safe Play compliance per the USTA requirements, including regular training and background checks. Ideally, all USTAF staff and program partners will be CPR/First Aid certified, including AED.
Budget Oversight: Manage the USTAF operational budget in collaboration with the leadership of the Programs and Services team of the USTA Foundation.
Grant Compliance: Assist partners in meeting the reporting requirements and performance benchmarks tied to USTA Foundation Program activities and funding
Ensure the program's compliance with all applicable Lulu’s Place youth safety policies, background check requirements, and licensing standards
Establish and oversee data collection, record-keeping, and reporting systems for student participation and outcomes across all program functions
Oversee vendor and service provider relationships (transportation, curriculum materials, technology, etc.)
In addition to the stated compliance and administration duties, review and maintain organizational policies and procedures, updating as needed to reflect best practices and legal requirements
Manage three full-time direct reports

Who You Are

Education: A bachelor’s degree in a related field such as Sports Management, Recreation Administration, Education, Social Work, or Non-Profit Management is required.
Work Experience: 5 to 7 years of experience in program coordination, youth development, or sports administration. Tennis background and/or understanding of the tennis environment is preferred.
Partner Management: Proven track record of managing relationships with community partners, schools, or diverse local organizations is required.
Safety Certifications: Valid CPR, First Aid, and AED certifications (or the ability to obtain them within 30 days of hire) are required.
Clearance: Ability to pass comprehensive, recurring federal and state background checks to work with minors is required.
Technical Proficiency: Strong skills in Microsoft Office Suite (especially Excel), Google Workspace, and familiarity with project management or participant tracking software are required.
Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation for travel between facility sites is required.
Schedule Flexibility: Ability to work non-traditional hours, including evenings and weekends, to align with youth sports schedules is required.
Physical Stamina: Ability to be mobile and active on sports courts or fields for extended periods and lift/move equipment up to 50 lbs is required.

What We Offer

At the USTA, we know people are our most important asset. For this reason, we offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to meet the needs of a diverse workforce!

Flexibility: Our Hybrid with Flexibility approach combines a balance of remote working with in-office collaboration to spark teamwork and creativity.
Comprehensive benefits designed to meet your unique needs: Medical, dental, vision, access to doctors virtually, a flexible spending account to manage your health and dependent care expenses, and life and disability insurance are a small part of our offerings.
Time to recharge and energize: Generous paid time off policy - including vacation, sick, personal, and paid holidays, parental leave, and a paid winter recess.
Plan for your future financially and professionally: 401(k) with employer matching (up to 6.5%), promotional and growth opportunities, Learning and Development programs to learn on the job, and up to $7,000 for tuition reimbursement.
Mental and emotional wellness: Resources for overall well-being, including mental health and meditation benefits.
Other cool perks: A personalized health management program, pet insurance, commuter benefits, identity theft protection, discounts with our network of partners, and fun events are just a few of the optional benefits available.

The expected range for the annual base salary for this position is $85,000 - 105,000.
This role is eligible for an Incentive Compensation Plan (ICP) bonus up to 10%. This range does not include any additional pay or benefits for which a person may qualify. The actual base salary offered is determined by several variables, including, as appropriate, the applicant's qualifications for the position, the years of relevant experience, their unique skills, and the location from which they will be performing the job.

Come One, Come All

We strongly encourage you to apply if you’re interested; we'd love to learn how you can “serve” our team with your unique experience!

USTA is dedicated to providing equal employment opportunities for all individuals, regardless of age, disability, national origin, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, or expression, pregnancy, veteran status, marital status, family status, alienage or citizenship status, creed, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

jobs.title: Project Rebound Program Director (Administrator I)
jobs.description:
This position is only open to Sonoma State University Employees

Application Process

This position is open until filled. For full consideration, please submit application, along with cover letter and resume, by 8am on Wednesday, October 21st.

Please review the positio n description listed above for full scope of responsibilities and qualifications.

Job Summary

Reporting to the Director of Equity and Access Programs, the Project Rebound Program Director provides management and guidance in support of the recruitment and success of formerly incarcerated students transitioning into higher education and supervises staff and student personnel. The incumbent supports a broad range of projects involving the development, planning, assessment and execution of programmatic and operational needs, including budget oversight and operational efficiency and effectiveness. The incumbent serves as a strategic partner and liaison with campus and community resources, advocating for program participants and managing the coordination of wraparound student support services. The incumbent ensures compliance with university and program policies, coordinates student services for academic and career success, and assists in the management of program operations and personnel.

Key Qualifications

This position requires three years of progressively responsible professional experience in educational or student support services, with at least one year of experience in program management or coordination, including 1 year of progressively responsible and applicable management and/or supervisory experience. Bachelor’s degree in education, counseling, social work, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred. Must possess demonstrated ability to support and advocate for underrepresented and underserved populations, particularly formerly incarcerated individuals. Experience building partnerships with community organizations and stakeholders highly preferred. Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and Google Workspace; familiarity with PeopleSoft and EAB Navigate preferred.

Salary And Benefits

Starting salary placement depends on qualifications and experience and is anticipated to be in th e range of $6,000- $6,250 a month. This position is a member of the Management Personnel Plan and serves at the pleasure of the President. This position is eligible for a broad range of benefits, including medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurances, retirement (CalPERS), tuition waiver, vacation and sick leave. In addition, 15 paid holidays are offered each year and a Personal Holiday that may be taken any time during the year. Sonoma State University is also a Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program (PSLF) Employer ( comprehensive benefits summary PDF ).

Supplemental Information

About Sonoma State University

Sonoma State University is committed to achieving excellence through teaching, scholarship, learning and inclusion. In line with our Strategic Plan and our Seawolf Commitment, our values include diversity, sustainability, community engagement, respect, responsibility, excellence and integrity. We strive to cultivate a community in which a diverse population can learn and work in an atmosphere of civility and respect. We encourage innovation, experimentation and creativity, as well as contributions to equity and inclusion, in the pursuit of excellence for all members of our university community.

Equal Opportunity & Mandated Reporting

The University is an Affirmative Action/Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, ancestry, age, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, genetic information, medical condition, disability, marital status, or protected veteran status. Mandated Reporting: This position may be considered a "mandated reporter" under the California Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act and is required to comply with the requirements set forth in CSU Executive Order 1083 as a condition of employment.

Employment Eligibility & Conditions

CSU Out of State Policy - Sonoma State University, as part of the CSU system, is a State of California Employer. As such, the University requires all employees upon date of hire to reside in the State of California. As of January 1, 2022 the CSU Out-of-State Employment Policy prohibits the hiring of employees to perform CSU-related work outside the state of California. A background check (including a criminal records check) must be completed satisfactorily before any candidate can be offered a position. Failure to satisfactorily complete the background check may affect the application status of applicants or continued employment of current employees who apply for this position.

Education Code 89521 - Applicants will be required to disclose whether they have received a final administrative decision or final judicial decision determining that they have committed sexual harassment within the last 7 years only after a determination is made that they meet the minimum qualifications for the position, and before an offer of employment is extended. Applicants who reach the final stages of the application process must also sign a release form that authorizes the release of information by the applicant’s current and/or former employers to the CSU concerning any substantiated allegations of misconduct.

Sonoma State University is not a sponsoring agency for staff positions (i.e. H-1B visas).

Positions are posted for a minimum of 14 calendar days.

Application Process & Accommodations

For questions related to the application process, please reach out to hr@sonoma.edu . The ADA Coordinator is also available ( hraccommodations@sonoma.edu ) to assist individuals with disabilities in need of accommodation during the hiring process.

Annual Reports & Safety Information

Sonoma State University's Annual Security Report (https://clery.sonoma.edu/annual-security-report) includes summaries of institutional policy relating to campus safety, drug and alcohol use, sexual assault, and other matters. The report is published in compliance with the Clery Act and includes three years of certain crime statistics that occurred in Clery Act defined geography. A paper copy of the report may be requested in person by emailing the Clery Compliance and Safety Office at clery@sonoma.edu .

Pursuant to the Higher Education Opportunity Act, the Annual Fire Safety Report (AFSR) is available for viewing at https://housing.sonoma.edu/compliance-data/2024-campus-housing-fire-safety-report . The purpose of this report is to disclose statistics for fires that occurred within Sonoma State University student housing facilities for three years, and to distribute fire safety policies and procedures intended to promote safety on campus. A paper copy of the AFSR is available upon request by contacting the Residential Education and Campus Housing at housing@sonoma.edu .

jobs.title: Assistant Director of Development, Corporate & Foundation Relations
jobs.description:
Join the vibrant community at California State University, Long Beach (CSULB)!

Located just three miles from the Pacific Ocean, CSULB offers an inspiring workplace and an exceptional Southern California lifestyle. Our 322-acre campus—one of the largest in the CSU system—serves more than 42,000 students and is known for its commitment to student success, innovation, and impactful academic and research initiatives.

As a member of the CSULB community, you’ll experience a dynamic environment filled with cultural landmarks, collaborative energy, and opportunities to make a meaningful difference.

Work-life balance thrives here. Long Beach blends coastal relaxation with urban vibrancy, offering miles of beaches, year-round sunshine, a thriving arts and food scene, and convenient access to both Los Angeles and Orange County. It’s an ideal place to grow your career while enjoying everything Southern California has to offer.

Join the California State University (CSU) and explore career opportunities that advance student success and strengthen California’s future—offering competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and professional growth.

Job Summary

The Assistant Director of Corporate & Foundation Relations develops and manages a portfolio of corporate and private foundation prospects and partners to secure philanthropic support for university priorities. The position collaborates with university leadership, faculty, and staff to identify funding opportunities, develop competitive proposals, cultivate and steward relationships, and advance strategic fundraising initiatives that support the university’s mission.

Key Responsibilities

Build and independently manage a portfolio of corporate and foundation prospects, driving all phases of the development life cycle: identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and renewal, with responsibility for securing annual renewals and new entry- and mid-level philanthropic investments in support of university priorities.
Collaborate with faculty and campus partners to research, write, coordinate, and submit grant applications, proposals, and letters of inquiry, with a focus on entry- and mid-level awards ranging from $10,000 to $75,000. Lead the proposal development process with grant seekers and ensure alignment with university policies, approval requirements, and gift and grant compliance standards.
Lead prospect cultivation and stewardship activities, including campus visits, in-person and virtual meetings, presentation materials for corporate and foundation representatives, and the development of impact reports. Create and maintain the CFR LinkedIn page to promote external philanthropic engagement, and produce the CFR Grant Opportunities Digest to increase campus awareness of philanthropic opportunities and application deadlines.

Department

University Development

Time Base

1.0 time-base, 40 hours per week.

Duration of Appointment

This is a temporary position for one year with no permanent status granted. Temporary assignments may expire prior to the ending date.

Classification

Advancement Professional II

Compensation

Salary placement is determined by the education, experience, and qualifications the candidate brings to the position, internal equity, and the hiring department’s fiscal resources.

Hiring Range: The hiring range for this position is $5,274 (Step #1) - $6,303(Step #10) per month commensurate with candidate's education, experience, skills, and training.
CSU Classification Salary Range: The CSU Classification Salary Range for this position is $5,274 (Step #1) - $7,684 (Step #20) per month.

Benefits

At California State University (CSU), we prioritize the health, growth, and success of our employees. Our benefits program reflects our commitment to your overall well-being.

To Be Eligible For Full Benefits, Employees Must Be Appointed At Least Half-time (.50 FTE) With An Appointment Lasting More Than Six Months And One Day. Benefits Eligibility And Offerings May Vary Based On Appointment Type, Classification, And Applicable Collective Bargaining Agreement. Eligible Employees May Have Access To a Comprehensive Benefits Package That Can Include:

Paid Time Off: Up to 24 vacation days per year (based on employee group and/or length of service), 14 paid holidays, and 12 sick days annually with unlimited accrual.
Health Coverage: A variety of medical, dental, and vision plans.
Retirement Plans: Participation in the CalPERS defined benefit plan, along with voluntary savings options such as 403(b), 401(k), and 457 plans.
Educational Benefits: Tuition fee waiver programs for eligible employees; dependent eligibility varies by employee group and bargaining unit.
Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.
Additional Benefits: Wellness programs, professional development opportunities, and insurance options including life, disability, and pet insurance.

Candidates are encouraged to review the appropriate CSU Employee Benefits Summary for details specific to their position. Additionally, the CSU Total Compensation Calculator is available to help prospective employees understand the full value of the CSU benefits package and how it complements base salary.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Strong organizational skills and meticulous attention to detail. Handles tasks with grace and committed to providing quality customer service. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Strong and consistent work ethic and professionalism complimented by a positive attitude and a commitment to diversity, openness, flexibility and integrity. Ability to solicit donations both verbally and in writing via email and/or letter. Ability to travel locally to meet with prospective donors. Ability to establish and maintain good working relationships with a variety of people - volunteers, prospects, donors, faculty, staff, students, and vendors. Ability to be discrete in handling confidential information.

Ability to perform clerical work involving sound judgment, accuracy and efficiency. Establish and maintain collaborative working relationships with program staff, academic departments, the Vice President’s office, and a variety of offices and individuals on and off campus. Working knowledge of Windows, Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams, Zoom, Power Point, Google Docs, Adobe Acrobat, Canva, CRM databases, grant research databases, and social media platforms like LinkedIn.` Ability to communicate with an ethnically and culturally diverse campus community. Experience building a trusted client network and generating revenue as a client-facing principal in wealth management, consulting or business development.

jobs.title: Chief Development Officer, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
"the Great Educational Equalizer"

— Philosopher Johnathan Bi, on Alpha School

Alpha is hiring.

You went into private school leadership to shape how children learn, not to run capital campaigns and referee parent committees. There is a version of this job where the academic model is protected for you, operations is handled centrally, and you spend your week on what you are best at: winning over the families who matter most, turning them into advocates, and being the voice of authority when the conversation gets hard.

You will own the parent side of Alpha in one metro — Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles. Your measure is enrollment and advocacy: prospective ultra-high-net-worth families who convert, current UHNW families who re-enroll, refer, and publicly champion 2 Hour Learning, and a local community where Alpha is top of mind. Roughly half your week is outward-facing — community partnerships, info sessions, and 1:1 conversations with sophisticated parents who have read every AI skeptic and want to know why the model actually works.

The rest of the seat is the escalation line. When an Associate Dean of Parents reaches the edge of what they can resolve — a board family threatening to pull their kids, a campus quietly softening the model to keep a vocal parent happy — it comes to you. You retain the family, and you keep the model intact. Both. Then you document the precedent so the Associate Dean network can handle it next time without you.

If you have run a private or independent K-12 school, or you have spent a career earning the trust of UHNW families in another industry, and you have been waiting for the job where judgment and persuasion are the actual deliverables, this is it.

What You Will Be Doing

Building local awareness through partnerships with family offices, private clubs, and independent advisors, plus workshops and community events that generate inbound interest
Running admissions for wealthy families end to end: info sessions, 1:1 follow-up in the CRM, and the enrollment decision, including telling a family this is not the right school for their child
Turning enrolled parents into public champions of 2 Hour Learning through advocacy workshops and parent-to-parent networks, so enrolled families become your strongest source of new inquiries
Resolving the escalations others cannot: diagnosing whether the problem is the model, campus execution, or family fit, engaging the family directly, then writing up the precedent for the rest of the network
Keeping current families close through regular touchpoints, and reporting the patterns you hear back to leadership

What You Won’t Be Doing

Capital campaigns, donor cultivation, major gifts, and every other form of fundraising are off your plate entirely
Convening PTAs, School Improvement Councils, parent committees, or focus groups that get a vote on school policy
Managing facilities, finance, legal, vendors, technology, marketing, or community logistics — centralized teams own all of this, so your week stays on relationships, not operations
Designing curriculum or coaching instructional staff on pedagogy; the academic model is owned and protected centrally
Making exceptions or customizations to the educational model to satisfy a parent request, however influential the parent
Simply logging and responding to complaints, or writing newsletters and routine parent communications
Defusing conflict by avoiding it — diplomacy here means delivering hard messages, not softening standards
Working behind the scenes; this is an on-site, full-time, face-of-the-school seat that includes evening and weekend community events

Chief Development Officer Key Responsibilities

Build a metro where Alpha families are 2 Hour Learning’s loudest advocates — and where no parent crisis is resolved by compromising the model.

Basic Requirements

7+ years leading high-stakes relationships in private or independent K-12 education, fundraising or major gifts, enterprise sales, client success, or private wealth management
2+ years working directly and regularly with ultra-high-net-worth or similarly high-expectation families, such as full-pay families at an elite private school, family-office clients, wealth-management clients, or major donors
Proven ownership of measurable enrollment, retention, advocacy, sales, or client outcomes, including resolving sensitive situations and holding firm standards when influential people push back
Polished executive communication, consultative judgment, and genuine conviction in Alpha's accelerated learning model, with the confidence to represent it to skeptical parents and public stakeholders
Living in the Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles metro area; authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship; and available for full-time on-site work, including 2 to 4 evening or weekend events per month

Nice-to-have Requirements

Sitting or recent Head of School — or the Head’s right hand — at a top-tier independent K-12 (NAIS-member or peer tier)
Multi-campus or multi-site school leadership experience (regional director, network superintendent, COO of a school network)
A UHNW client-services background translated into school leadership: private wealth management, single-family office, or major-gifts development at an elite prep or Ivy
An existing network among UHNW families or influential local organizations in Miami, San Francisco, or Los Angeles
Crisis communication experience involving press, regulators, or board-level stakeholders
Hands-on AI building experience — custom GPTs, agents, or vibe-coded internal tools used in a real operating context
An advanced degree (M.Ed., MBA, or doctorate) — common in this profile, but not required; no formal education is required for this role

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

jobs.title: Director of External Relations, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
Families often come to Alpha through recommendations from people they trust. You will lead the regional relationships that support this growth, connect families and create opportunities for students.

You will design and host gatherings, from eight-person dinners to 150-person open houses; develop a network of parent ambassadors; and build relationships with public officials and business leaders. Through Alpha Networks, you will arrange introductions, expert masterclasses and internships, and welcome graduating families into the alumni community.

You will develop, document and improve the region’s working methods while delivering its programs, sharing effective practices with colleagues in other cities. Success will be measured by the share of enrollment growth generated through personal referrals over several years. The number of introductions and opportunities created per family must also increase as enrollment grows.

A degree is not required for every candidate, but your background must include at least one of the academic, professional or civic qualifications listed below. You also need a record of bringing people together and producing tangible results through those relationships.

The role is on site in Miami, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Boston, Dallas or New York City. It requires regular local travel and hosting commitments on weekday evenings and weekends.

What You Will Be Doing

Plan and deliver several gatherings each month, including open events, dinners organized by city and grade, and family retreats, within budget.
Secure venues, hosts and vendors, and personally host events.
Recruit current parents as ambassadors, help them share their experiences, and match them with prospective families, including those attending school tours.
Build relationships with public officials and business executives to secure venues, support for new campus openings and opportunities for students.
Connect enrolled families with parent circles and students with mentors, masterclasses and practical internships. Welcome graduating families into the alumni community within 30 days of graduation.
Record every gathering and introduction, and how each family first heard about Alpha, in the customer relationship management (CRM) system. Maintain accurate records of the introductions and opportunities created for each family.

What You Won’t Be Doing

Manage paid advertising or work to targets for impressions or lead volume.
Lead brand communications or central marketing campaigns; these are Marketing’s responsibility.
Process admissions, conduct tours or manage enrollment paperwork; these are the responsibilities of Admissions and Family Success.
Run daily campus operations or manage the opening of physical premises.
Treat attendance figures alone as evidence of success.
Rely on a completed operating manual, templates or support staff to begin work.

Director Of External Relations Key Responsibilities

Make personal referrals the source of the majority of enrollment growth in your region.

Basic Requirements

At least five years of experience growing a community or client base through relationships, with at least one result you personally drove that you can explain with a number and a timeframe.
Experience personally designing and running at least 20 gatherings in total, including at least three events with 100 or more attendees and ten gatherings with 12 or fewer people, with responsibility for budgets.
Established working relationships with at least three elected or appointed public officials, C-level executives or centaur-company founders, with specific results from those relationships. You can host senior audiences, explain a new education model under questioning, and build partnerships that benefit both sides while respecting voluntary participation and compliance rules.
At least one of these qualifications: an Ivy League degree; work at a top consulting, investment banking or public relations firm; a board seat at a local anchor institution; Chief of Staff experience with political or major industry leaders; or directed tours in the foreign service.
Consistent use of a CRM or relationship-tracking system to record contacts, how families first heard about the organization, follow-ups and actions, with accurate first-contact records that remain unchanged.
A deep local network you can use from day one in Miami, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Boston, Dallas or New York City, and residence in or willingness to return or relocate to that region. You must be available for regular weekday-evening and weekend hosting and local travel, and authorized to work in the United States without visa sponsorship.

Nice-to-have Requirements

Experience leading regional growth, community programs or partnerships for a school group, membership club, franchise, faith or civic institution, or similar organization.
Experience building a trusted client network and generating revenue as a client-facing principal in wealth management, consulting or business development.
A background in admissions, advancement, community organizing or hospitality, with experience hosting events and representing an institution.
Established relationships with local government or business leaders in your region.
An understanding of how families make important decisions about their children’s education.

WD is building the infrastructure behind the AI-driven data economy.

As AI scales, so does data. Every interaction, every model, every system generates data that must be stored, managed, and made accessible over time. That’s where we come in.

We combine deep engineering expertise with global-scale manufacturing to deliver the storage systems that make AI possible, powering hyperscale data centers, cloud platforms, and enterprise infrastructure worldwide.

This isn’t theoretical work. It’s real systems, at real scale, people solving some of the hardest challenges in technology today.

We’re looking for people who want to build, solve, and operate at that level.

Join us and let’s shape the future of data.

Job Description

We are seeking an experienced, creative and highly versatile communications professional to join our Strategic Communications team as Senior Manager, Strategic Communications, CEO & Strategy.

This role will be a key partner in supporting and strengthening communications for WD’s CEO, working closely with Strategic Communications leadership to help execute and continually strengthen the CEO communications program. The Senior Manager will take on significant responsibility for day-to-day content development while contributing fresh ideas and perspectives to the broader CEO communications strategy. This person will develop executive content across formats and channels, help shape the story and flow for key engagements, and continually look for new and more effective ways to communicate.

The role will also serve as communications partner to WD’s Strategy organization, helping translate company strategy and business priorities into clear, compelling communications. The ideal candidate is an exceptional writer and creative storyteller who combines strong executive communications instincts with curiosity, judgment and a willingness to challenge conventional approaches.

Essential Duties & Key Responsibilities

CEO Communications & Storytelling

Manage a broad range of day-to-day CEO communications deliverables across internal and external audiences, including talking points, presentations, emails, video scripts, briefing materials, and social content.
Help shape the story, narrative flow, and creative approach for CEO keynotes, company meetings, videos, and other executive engagements.
Partner with Strategic Communications leadership to help advance the CEO communications strategy, bring fresh ideas and identify opportunities to strengthen the CEO’s platform, extend key narratives and engage audiences in new ways.
Bring fresh thinking to executive communications, exploring new formats, channels and approaches rather than defaulting to how things have traditionally been done.
Manage day-to-day CEO social content, including identifying opportunities and developing content.
Partner closely with the CEO Office and stakeholders across the company to develop briefing materials and prepare the CEO for key engagements.
Help maintain consistency in the CEO’s voice and messaging while looking for opportunities to make communications more authentic, compelling, and effective.

Strategy Communications

Serve as the day-to-day communications partner to the Strategy organization and its leadership.
Help translate WD’s strategy, priorities and direction into clear, engaging communications for key audiences.
Support Strategy leaders with presentations, talking points, leadership updates, and other communications needs.
Connect Strategy and CEO communications, helping ensure the company’s strategic direction is reflected consistently and brought to life through compelling stories and examples.

Cross-Functional Partnership & Execution

Build trusted relationships with the CEO Office, Strategy and partners across Communications, Marketing, Investor Relations and other functions.
Manage multiple workstreams simultaneously, taking communications from initial concept through review and final execution.
Anticipate needs, surface opportunities and bring recommendations rather than waiting for direction.
Provide flexible support across Strategic Communications during high-priority company moments as needed.

Qualifications

Required

8+ years of experience in executive communications, corporate communications, strategic communications, or a related field.
Experience supporting senior executives and developing C-suite-level communications.
Exceptional writing, editing and storytelling skills across executive presentations, talking points, emails, video, briefing materials and social content.
Demonstrated ability to bring creative ideas and new approaches to communications, not simply execute established programs or formats.
Strong ability to translate complex business and strategic topics into clear, compelling narratives.
Excellent judgment, discretion, and executive presence.
Strong project management skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities and fast-turn requests without sacrificing quality.
Ability to work independently, anticipate needs, and navigate ambiguity.
Strong collaboration and stakeholder management skills.
Strong PowerPoint and visual storytelling skills.

Preferred

Experience directly supporting a CEO or C-suite executive.
Experience communicating corporate strategy, transformation or other complex business topics.
Experience in technology or another fast-moving industry.

Creative thinker: Brings original ideas and challenges conventional approaches.
Exceptional storyteller: Knows how to find the story in complex material and make it resonate.
Strategic and hands-on: Can think about the bigger picture and then personally create the content that delivers it.
Proactive and opinionated in the right way: Brings recommendations and a point of view rather than simply taking direction.
Curious and adaptable: Constantly looks for better ways to communicate and is comfortable changing course as priorities evolve.
Trusted collaborator: Builds strong relationships, welcomes different perspectives and feedback, and stays focused on getting to the best outcome.

jobs.description:
Are you looking to join an organization that is growing and dynamic? What about a high-energy, collaborative environment that rewards hard work?

J.S. Held is a global consulting firm providing technical, scientific, and financial expertise. Our professionals serve as trusted advisors to organizations facing high-stakes events demanding urgent attention, staunch integrity, and clear-cut analysis. The firm provides a comprehensive suite of services enabling clients to navigate complex, contentious, and often catastrophic situations. We have over 100 locations worldwide. We are highly committed to all members of our community, both employees and clients. Our organization focuses on promoting a sense of community and inspiring our people to achieve results that exceed goals.

Job Description

We are seeking a Managing Director to join our Strategic Advisory Group. This is a unique opportunity for an entrepreneurial, highly driven person with a well-rounded skill set to join the Strategic Advisory Group. The ideal person for this role will need to have significant demonstrated experience in operational turnarounds and financial restructurings both in and out of bankruptcy court as well as within the context of Receiverships and Assignments for the Benefit of Creditors, and a strong grasp of the lending and M&A markets. This person will be a leader, who can think strategically, develop and implement a plan, and keep all the parties moving forward to effectuate the plan – generally during a crisis when there is a lack of human and financial resources.

J.S. Held’s Strategic Advisory Group helps distressed organizations stabilize operations, protect stakeholder interests, and execute turnaround strategies. We take an operationally focused approach that looks beyond the balance sheet to minimize further degradation and build a path to sustainable growth. Our team delivers hands-on guidance and independent analysis to lenders, creditors, legal counsel, executive teams, boards of directors, and investors.

Our Strategic Advisory Group has openings available at the Managing Director level. The candidate will join an experienced and closely-knit team of professionals, with deep experience in leading, planning and solving the most complex client situations. 

Job Responsibilities

Lead operational turnaround management and financial restructuring engagements;

Provide expertise and leadership in investment banking, valuation, litigation support and asset disposition roles of our clients;

Manage and lead teams of JS Held personnel;

Lead interaction with client teams, shareholders, lenders and other stakeholders

Manage multiple projects simultaneously;

Work under stress in crisis situations with limited resources and tight deadlines;

Produce deliverables;

Provide marketplace leading skills in business development efforts to develop and further cultivate both existing and new referral source relationships within the legal, lending and investor communities in generating revenue opportunities;

Collaborate with internal stakeholders to develop and implement go-to-to-market strategies related to driving revenue growth;

Provide support in other ad-hoc tasks as requested.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

20+ years of relevant work experience within the turnaround and restructuring marketplace both in leading assignments and demonstrated abilities for business development.

Ability to develop understanding and ability to cross-sell other JS Held expertise and service offerings both to existing and new referral source relationships.

Ability to delegate and lead multiple projects and mentor subordinate professional staff a must.

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college/university. Advanced degrees, such as JD or MBA, are a plus.

Strong organization and attention to detail skills.

Experienced working in challenging, often chaotic environments in leading client(s) to achieve the stated case(s) goals and objectives.

Knowledge of all aspects of bankruptcy is a must.

Able to multi-task and meet deadlines;

This position requires travel to clients, at times extensive.

Physical and Mental Job Qualifications

Travel as needed

Additional Information

Some of the Benefits We Have Include

J.S. Held understands all our employees are people and sometimes life needs flexibility. We work to always provide an environment that best supports and suits our team’s needs.

Our flexible work environment allows employees to work remotely, when needed

Flexible Time Off policy

Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance

401k Match

Commuter Benefit

A reasonable estimate of the salary range for this role is $300,000-$400,000. Any offered salary range is based on a wide array of factors including but not limited to skillset, experience, training, location, scope of role, management responsibility, etc.

Other Duties

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

By submitting your application, you acknowledge that you have read the J.S. Held Online Privacy Notice and hereby freely and unambiguously give informed consent to the collection, processing, use, and storage of your personal information as required and described therein. California residents can click here to learn more about the personal information we collect and here to learn about additional privacy rights that may be available.

Please explore what we’re all about at www.jsheld.com.

EEO and Job Accommodations

We embrace diversity and our commitment to building a team and environment that fosters professional and personal enrichment is unwavering. 

J.S. Held is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.

If you are an individual with a disability and would like to request a reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process, please email jobs@jsheld.com. Include "Applicant Accommodation" in the subject line, along with your request and contact information.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Director of Community Engagement, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
"Alpha School students, on average, experience 2.4 to 2.6 times the academic growth of traditional school students"

— Forbes

Alpha is hiring.

Families often come to Alpha through recommendations from people they trust. You will lead the regional relationships that support this growth, connect families and create opportunities for students.

You will design and host gatherings, from eight-person dinners to 150-person open houses; develop a network of parent ambassadors; and build relationships with public officials and business leaders. Through Alpha Networks, you will arrange introductions, expert masterclasses and internships, and welcome graduating families into the alumni community.

You will develop, document and improve the region’s working methods while delivering its programs, sharing effective practices with colleagues in other cities. Success will be measured by the share of enrollment growth generated through personal referrals over several years. The number of introductions and opportunities created per family must also increase as enrollment grows.

No degree or prescribed career path is required. Relevant experience may come from consulting, wealth management, community work, hospitality or advancement. What matters is a record of bringing people together and producing tangible results through those relationships.

The role is on site in Miami, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Boston, Dallas or New York City. It requires regular local travel and hosting commitments on weekday evenings and weekends.

What You Will Be Doing

As Director of Community Engagement, plan and deliver several gatherings each month, including open events, dinners organized by city and grade, and family retreats, within budget.
Secure venues, hosts and vendors, and personally host events.
Recruit current parents as ambassadors, help them share their experiences, and match them with prospective families, including those attending school tours.
Build relationships with public officials and business executives to secure venues, support for new campus openings and opportunities for students.
Connect enrolled families with parent circles and students with mentors, masterclasses and practical internships. Welcome graduating families into the alumni community within 30 days of graduation.
Record every gathering and introduction, and how each family first heard about Alpha, in the customer relationship management (CRM) system. Maintain accurate records of the introductions and opportunities created for each family.

What You Won’t Be Doing

Manage paid advertising or work to targets for impressions or lead volume.
Lead brand communications or central marketing campaigns; these are Marketing’s responsibility.
Process admissions, conduct tours or manage enrollment paperwork; these are the responsibilities of Admissions and Family Success.
Run daily campus operations or manage the opening of physical premises.
Treat attendance figures alone as evidence of success.
Rely on a completed operating manual, templates or support staff to begin work.

Director Of Community Engagement Key Responsibilities

Make personal referrals the source of the majority of enrollment growth in your region.

Basic Requirements

At least five years’ experience building communities or relationship programs in K–12 education, membership organizations or a comparable business, with measurable growth through referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni or client relationships.
Experience personally designing and delivering at least 20 gatherings, ranging from small dinners to open events with more than 100 attendees, with responsibility for budgets.
A record of building and maintaining relationships with public officials or business executives that produced specific, demonstrable results.
Consistent use of a CRM or relationship-tracking system to record contacts, how families first heard about the organization, follow-ups and actions.
An established local network in Miami, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Boston, Dallas or New York City, and residence in—or willingness to return or relocate to—that region.
Availability to host regularly on weekday evenings and weekends, and to travel locally.
Authorization to work in the United States without visa sponsorship.

Nice-to-have Requirements

Experience leading regional growth, community programs or partnerships for a school group, membership club, franchise, faith or civic institution, or similar organization.
Experience building a trusted client network and generating revenue as a client-facing principal in wealth management, consulting or business development.
A background in admissions, advancement, community organizing or hospitality, with experience hosting events and representing an institution.
Established relationships with local government or business leaders in your region.
An understanding of how families make important decisions about their children’s education.

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

The compensation level for this role is $400,000 USD/year. The payment period is weekly. Consult www.crossover.com/help-and-faqs for more details on this topic.

jobs.title: Business Development Director
jobs.description:
Premier firm with strong entrepreneurial spirit
Highly visible role and leading strategy for revenue-oriented initiatives

About Our Client

Our client is a New York-based mid-sized business law firm with a national reputation in capital markets, securities, M&A, litigation, and financial services, known for handling sophisticated matters typically associated with much larger firms. The firm is recognized for combining high-level legal expertise with an entrepreneurial, client-focused approach.

Job Description

Serve as the firm's senior marketing and business development leader, working directly with the Management Committee, practice leaders, and partners.
Develop and execute firmwide and practice-specific business development plans aligned with growth objectives.
Create and oversee high-quality pitches, proposals, RFP responses, capability statements, and other client-facing materials.
Build sophisticated PowerPoint presentations and executive-level marketing collateral under tight deadlines.
Establish and maintain consistent branding standards across all firm communications and marketing assets.
Manage the firm's website, attorney bios, social media presence, and external marketing vendors.
Prepare attorneys for client pitches and business development meetings through research, strategy, messaging, and follow-up planning.
Drive cross-selling initiatives and help attorneys build disciplined, accountable business development habits.
Oversee conferences, sponsorships, speaking engagements, and client events, including budgeting, logistics, and ROI measurement.
Track pipeline activity, proposal results, CRM data, rankings submissions, and marketing performance metrics, providing actionable reporting to leadership.

This role will be based in firm's New York office.

The Successful Applicant

A Successful Business Development Director Should Have

7+ years of marketing and business development experience, ideally within a law firm environment
Experience partnering directly with firm leadership, practice leaders, and other senior stakeholders
Proven success developing pitches and proposals that have resulted in new business and client wins
Expert-level PowerPoint and presentation design skills, with strong writing and visual communication capabilities
Experience with CRM platforms such as Salesforce and broader marketing technology tools
Working knowledge of digital marketing, website management, email marketing, analytics, and business intelligence resources
Strong executive presence, project management skills, and the ability to influence attorneys and drive initiatives without direct authority

What's on Offer

The salary range for this role is $180,000 to $210,000 USD for New York.

This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee's position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance.

The successful candidate may be eligible for annual discretionary bonus.

The firm offers a comprehensive package of benefits including Paid Time Off, medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k) with safe harbor match to eligible employees.

This role requires in-office presence 4 days/week including Mondays as mandatory.

Contact: Megan McArdle

jobs.title: Youth Development Director, Alpha - $200,000/year USD
jobs.description:
"We are never going to lower the standard for any kid — instead we're going to raise the support to help them get there."

— Braden, Head Guide, Alpha Austin

Alpha is hiring.

In person at an Alpha campus in New York City, NY or Miami, FL; relocation support provided
$200,000/year
Full-time

Most youth development programs respond to struggling kids by lowering expectations. You don't.

You believe young children are capable of far more than traditional programs ask of them, and you've built teams that prove it with measurable results. You know that motivation, accountability, and high standards change lives more than another worksheet ever will.

At Alpha, academics happen in just two hours each morning through adaptive learning technology. That frees you to focus on the work that has the biggest long-term impact: coaching students to become independent learners while developing the Guides who make that growth possible. You will own outcomes for a cohort of K-3 students, using data, observation, and coaching to ensure every child loves school, learns twice as fast, and develops exceptional life skills.

This is not an instructional coach role, nor a principal role. You won't spend your days buried in meetings or paperwork. You'll be in classrooms, analyzing student and Guide performance, delivering workshops on communication, resilience, focus, and accountability, and coaching both children and adults toward measurable improvement.

Your influence won't stop with your own cohort. You'll document what works, build playbooks that raise the standard across the school, and help shape how Alpha develops future Guides. If you're energized by building people, scaling excellence, and proving that extraordinary outcomes are possible when expectations stay high, we'd love to meet you.

What You Will Be Doing

Coach Guides and students using performance data, classroom observations, and direct feedback to achieve measurable improvements.
Facilitate engaging workshops for K-3 students focused on communication, resilience, collaboration, accountability, focus, and other life skills.
Lead one-on-one and small-group coaching sessions that connect student motivation to academic growth and independence.
Build and refine repeatable coaching playbooks that raise performance across the Guide team.
Train and mentor Guides while modeling exceptional coaching and facilitation every day.

What You Won’t Be Doing

Delivering traditional classroom instruction or lecturing through academic content; adaptive technology handles core academics.
Managing discipline through punishment or lowering expectations when students struggle.
Leading from an office instead of working directly with students and Guides every day.
Owning campus operations, budgets, or parent communications; your focus is developing people and improving outcomes.
Following conventional elementary school practices simply because "that's how schools have always done it."

Youth Development Director Key Responsibilities

Deliver Alpha's three promises for every K-3 student by building high-performing Guides, highly motivated students, and a coaching culture that consistently produces exceptional academic and life outcomes.

Basic Requirements

Willing to work in person at an Alpha campus in New York City, NY or Miami, FL; relocation support is provided.
Bachelor's degree in Education, Psychology, Business, Organizational Leadership, Child Development, or a related field.
At least 5 years of experience working with elementary-aged children (approximately ages 5-9).
Experience leading teams of five or more people, including performance management and hiring decisions.
Experience building, launching, or significantly growing a program, school, team, or initiative rather than maintaining an existing one.
Demonstrated success using data and measurable outcomes to improve team or student performance.
Compelling storytelling and facilitation skills that engage young children, plus the ability to coach adults with clear expectations and direct feedback.
Excited by challenging conventional education models and embracing a coaching-first approach.
Legally authorized to work in the United States.

Nice-to-have Requirements

Master's degree in a related field.
Experience using dashboards, analytics, or performance metrics to drive continuous improvement.
Track record of coaching adults toward measurable performance outcomes.
Background in youth development, competitive coaching, enrichment programs, camps, or other high-accountability environments.
Strong public speaking and facilitation skills with young children.

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.
