jobs.title: Michigan Executive Director and Midwest Partner
jobs.description:
What We Can Achieve Together

The Michigan Executive Director and Midwest Partner functions as a leader and conservation strategist for a large, complex business unit in a global organization that plays an integral leadership role in TNC’s Midwest Division. The Midwest Division encompasses Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Ohio and Wisconsin—a region of Great Lakes, great rivers and immense global importance for conserving biodiversity, tackling climate change, and protecting lands and waters as outlined in TNC’s 2030 goals. In addition to representing Michigan and the Midwest, this position must also be versed in national and global TNC priorities.

This position will be a key leader in a global fundraising campaign and is responsible for producing measurable conservation results, while leading a large, multidisciplinary team of professionals across the state. They serve as the primary spokesperson for TNC in Michigan to internal and external audiences (including public and private donors, media, the business community, the Michigan Board of Trustees, community leaders and other partners, government agencies and officials and staff). They cultivate those audiences to support and promote TNC’s mission and vision.

The Michigan Executive Director and Midwest Partner sets objectives and manages the performance of a large and collaborative team with a focus on strategy development, fundraising and managing the Board of Trustees. They work together across teams as they cultivate and solicit high-level donors (private and public) to meet fundraising goals. Additionally, this role supports conservation programs and initiatives, organization visibility, policy and government relations, the management of staff and the financial health of the business unit.

The Michigan Executive Director and Midwest Partner also collaborates with peer Midwest Executive Directors and the Midwest Division Director (known as the Midwest Board of Partners) in helping shape the strategy, development and execution of cross-boundary efforts within the Midwest and globally, including the contribution of financial and human resources. Along with other members of the Midwest Board of Partners, the Michigan Executive Director supports the Midwest 2030 conservation goals, and sponsors one or more conservation strategy and functional area teams at the regional level. They help align their team’s work to secure and deploy sufficient resources and capacity to achieve the Midwest’s maximum contribution to TNC’s 2030 conservation goals.

The Michigan Executive Director and Midwest Partner creates a healthy work environment for all TNC staff in the state and supports coordinated staff development across the region. This position reports to the Midwest Division Director and works in partnership with the Midwest Board of Partners and the Michigan Board of Trustees.

Location:
Within Michigan, preference for the greater Lansing, Ann Arbor, Detroit, or Grand Rapids areas.

We’re Looking For You

Are you looking for work that you can believe in? At TNC, we strive to embody a philosophy of “Work That You Can Believe In” where you can feel like you are making a difference every day. We’re looking for someone with strong experience leading a diverse, multidisciplinary team.

The ideal candidate should have exceptional leadership skills, with a strong background in high-level fundraising. They must be a compelling storyteller and talented communicator who can successfully use these talents to fundraise, build consensus and speak about TNC’s mission, vision and work—from state, regional and global perspective. This role must be able to effectively engage a wide range of partners, while constantly building and engaging the volunteer Board of Trustees.

This position requires a person with deep self-confidence tempered by genuine humility. They must have an ambitious yet collaborative nature. They must be very high-energy, intelligent, abstract thinkers willing to take bold, calculated risks while balancing the need to make transparent decisions in a matrixed and sometimes ambiguous environment. They must have very high emotional intelligence and be compassionate but also able to make tough decisions while being equitable, fair and inclusive.

This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the ongoing mission of conservation by directing and shaping the work of Michigan and the Midwest.

What You’ll Bring

Bachelor’s degree and minimum of 7 years of experience as a leader in the conservation arena, non-profit sector, advocacy, or related for-profit area.
Extensive management experience, including the ability to motivate, lead, set objectives and manage the performance of a large multidisciplinary team.
Proven experience in cultivating and soliciting high-level donors to reach fundraising goals, which is a priority for this position.
Written and verbal fluency in English.
Effective presentation and communication skills for diverse audiences, including high-level donors, the media, the business community, board members, outside partners, staff or equivalent that lead to desired outcomes.
Experience with strategic fiscal management, including long-term sustainability.

Desired Qualifications

Seven to 10 years of experience as a proven leader in the conservation arena, nonprofit sector, advocacy, or related for-profit area, including demonstrated experience producing results and meeting organizational, divisional or business unit goals.
Experience working in the U.S. and globally preferred. Demonstrated commitment to developing and practicing global literacy.
Outstanding leadership skills, including thought-leadership, visionary qualities and the ability to inspire others in a decentralized, geographically dispersed and highly matrixed organization.
Knowledge of conservation and conservation practices.
High energy, forward-thinking and creative individual with high ethical standards.
Proven strategic thinking skills, creative problem-solving, adept decision-making, adaptability and ability to collaborate and influence.
Demonstrated experience in public speaking on behalf of a global organization with the capability to present on a wide range of science-based and conservation topics desired.
A strong network of local, regional and national contacts that include leaders from philanthropic, business and communities relevant to our conservation work.

This position requires a valid driver's license and compliance with TNC’s Auto Safety Program
. Employees may not drive Conservancy-owned/leased vehicles, rental cars, or personal vehicles on behalf of the Conservancy if considered "high risk drivers." To learn more about the Auto Safety Program, visit the Auto Safety information page. Employment in this position will be contingent upon completion of a Vehicle Use Agreement, which may include a review of the prospective employee's motor vehicle record.

Salary Information

The starting pay range for a candidate selected for this position is generally within the range of $185,000 - $218,000. This range only applies to candidates whose country of employment is the USA. Where a successful candidate’s actual pay will fall within this range will be based on a variety of factors, including, for example, the candidate's location, qualifications, specific skills, and experience. Please note countries outside the USA would have a different pay range in the local currency based on the local labor market, and not tied to USA pay or ranges. Your geographic location will be confirmed during the recruitment.

Who We Are

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor.

One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”

What We Bring

Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

TNC offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package including health care benefits, flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) plan with an 8% employer match, parental leave, accrued paid time off, life insurance, disability coverage, employee assistance program, other life and work well-being benefits. Learn more about our Benefits and Perks here.

We’re proud to offer a flexible work environment that supports of the health and well-being of the people we employ.

Our recruiting process includes a rolling interview process to ensure we engage applicants in a timely manner. This means we may review applications in the order in which they are received. Once a strong candidate pool is identified, the role will be unposted. The timeline may vary depending on the expressed interest in the role, so we highly encourage candidates to apply as soon as possible.

The Nature Conservancy is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
Our commitment to equal employment opportunity includes the recognition that our conservation mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people of all backgrounds, beliefs, and culture. Recruiting and mentoring staff to create an inclusive organization is a priority, and we encourage applicants from all cultures, races, colors, religions, sexes, national or regional origins, ages, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity, military, protected veteran status or other status protected by law.

The successful applicant must meet the requirements of The Nature Conservancy's background screening process.

Do you have military experience? Visit our U.S. Military Skills Translator to match your military experience with our current job openings!

TNC is committed to offering accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application process. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please send a note to applyhelp@tnc.org with Request for Accommodation in the subject line.

FHI 360 is a nonprofit organization that mobilizes research, resources, and relationships so that people everywhere can access the opportunities they need to lead full, healthy lives. Our staff of more than 2,000 experts work in over 50 countries around the world. FHI 360’s Institute for Work & Learning (IWL) creates thriving community ecosystems by connecting people with career and growth opportunities. Our team designs, implements, and evaluates initiatives focused on career readiness and workforce development to help businesses gain talent and individuals build the skills and experience they need to progress in their career pathways, contribute to their communities, and live successful lives.

The Workforce Program Director will lead a multi-million-dollar portfolio of programs, including an array of corporate-funded, Department of Labor, and Department of Justice projects. This leadership position will report to IWL’s Learning & Workforce Development Portfolio Director and manage activities and oversee all program operations, provide strategic direction, support business development, and ensure compliance with policies and relevant regulations.

include but are not limited to :

Supports capacity building and contributes to IWL’s overall strategic goals and assigned projects.

Job Details

Description

At Heartland Family Service, we are committed to building a culture that is trauma informed and values and celebrates diversity and inclusion. We believe this allows for better service delivery and innovation, as it encourages our employees to bring various experiences and uniqueness to the workplace.

jobs.title: Chief Development Officer
jobs.description:
Chief Development Officer

Reports to
: President, OLYD
Role Type:
Executive Leadership
Compensation:
Founding, equity-only role at this stage; compensation is expected to evolve as OLYD's funding and revenue grow.

About OLYD

Oh! Love Ya Dawn (OLYD) is a shared movement where creativity, compassion, and purpose come together.

Through the Oh! Love Ya Dawn Company, we build products, platforms, and experiences that carry meaning and connection. Through our Foundation, we turn those efforts into programs that protect and uplift children who have experienced abuse or neglect.

Together, we are creating something that proves business can have a heartbeat and that structure and humanity can grow side by side.

Role Overview

OLYD is seeking an experienced, highly proactive Chief Development Officer (CDO) to build and lead our philanthropic funding strategy while remaining deeply engaged in the work.

This is not a purely strategic or administrative role. The CDO will personally cultivate donor relationships, develop funding opportunities, make significant asks, build fundraising systems, and move opportunities from idea to action.

The CDO will lead major gifts, individual giving, grants and institutional giving, corporate philanthropy, and donor development and stewardship.

We are looking for a leader who creates momentum.

The right person will assess where we are, determine what is needed, develop a path forward, engage the right people and resources, remove barriers, and keep the work moving.

Key Responsibilities

Philanthropic Strategy & Leadership

Build and execute a philanthropic funding strategy aligned with OLYD's mission, programs, growth priorities, and funding needs.
Establish clear fundraising goals, priorities, pipelines, timelines, and measures of success.
Create the systems and operating rhythm to move opportunities from identification through cultivation, solicitation, closing, and stewardship.
Lead team members supporting philanthropy, grants, donor engagement, and related development activities.
Establish ownership and accountability, identify obstacles early, and drive them toward resolution.
Give leadership a clear view of pipeline health, anticipated funding, risks, opportunities, and decisions needed.

Major Gifts & Donor Development

Personally identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward major individual donors and prospects.
Build and actively manage a strong major-gift pipeline rather than relying solely on existing OLYD relationships.
Develop donor strategies based on individual interests, capacity, connection to the mission, and stage of engagement.
Make significant philanthropic asks and guide other OLYD leaders through cultivation and solicitation when their involvement will strengthen an opportunity.
Activate the networks of OLYD leaders, board members, volunteers, partners, and supporters to expand our donor community.
Build long-term relationships that create sustained philanthropic engagement.

Grants & Institutional Giving

Lead a proactive institutional-giving strategy across private, family, and corporate foundations and other appropriate grantmakers.
Maintain a prioritized pipeline and calendar of grant opportunities, applications, reports, and renewals.
Provide clear direction and accountability to OLYD's grant-writing resources.
Coordinate cross-functional grant support from OLYD team members contributing expertise alongside their primary roles.
Keep grant opportunities moving by identifying missing information, setting owners and deadlines, and resolving barriers.
Partner with Program Development, Finance, and other experts to develop compelling, accurate, fundable proposals.
Ensure applications and reports are timely and OLYD meets its commitments to funders.

External Leadership & Representation

Serve as a credible philanthropic ambassador with donors, foundations, corporate partners, community leaders, and other stakeholders.
Represent OLYD independently in donor meetings, philanthropic events, networking opportunities, and presentations.
Understand OLYD's mission, programs, impact, and direction and communicate them authentically and persuasively.
Partner with the President to align organizational strategy, external positioning, and philanthropic priorities.
Engage and prepare the President, CEO, board members, program leaders, or other representatives when their involvement will strengthen an opportunity.
Help expand OLYD's visibility and credibility within philanthropic communities and networks.

Development Infrastructure & Stewardship

Evaluate current development practices and establish scalable processes, tools, and systems where needed.
Build disciplined practices for prospect management, donor records, relationship tracking, stewardship, and reporting.
Establish stewardship strategies that demonstrate impact, deepen relationships, and encourage continued engagement.
Partner across teams to ensure development materials clearly communicate OLYD's work and impact.
Build a development function that can grow with OLYD beyond individual relationships or one-time efforts.

How You'll Lead

At OLYD, leadership means more than directing others.

The CDO must be comfortable moving between strategy, leadership, and execution—whether developing a multi-year strategy, coaching a team member, reviewing the grant pipeline, resolving an obstacle, preparing another executive, or personally making the ask.

You are likely to thrive in this role if you:

Take ownership of outcomes, not simply activities.
Create clarity and momentum when the path forward is not fully defined.
Proactively identify what you need and ask for it rather than waiting for someone to check in.
Bring recommendations and solutions alongside problems.
Know when to involve others without unnecessarily handing work off.
Follow through consistently and expect the same from others.
Are comfortable holding peers and senior leaders accountable to commitments that affect development outcomes.
Balance urgency and accountability with kindness, respect, and strong relationships.
Are energized by building in an early-stage environment where roles, systems, and priorities continue to evolve.
Are adaptable and comfortable wearing multiple hats, collaborating across functions, and pitching in when your expertise can help move the organization forward.
Use good judgment and take initiative—building what is needed, making the most of what exists, and moving good ideas forward without unnecessary permission while keeping the right people informed and engaged.
Believe that being an executive leader and being willing to do the work are not mutually exclusive.

What You Bring

Required

Significant experience in nonprofit development, philanthropy, or institutional advancement, with increasing responsibility for strategy and results.
Success developing and executing philanthropic strategies that produced measurable funding growth.
A strong major-gift cultivation and solicitation record, including personally making significant donor asks.
Experience building and managing donor or prospect pipelines from identification through stewardship.
Institutional-giving and grant-development knowledge sufficient to lead and hold a grants function accountable.
Ability to build relationships with high-net-worth individuals, foundations, corporate philanthropic partners, and other funders.
Experience leading people and cross-functional initiatives through influence, accountability, and collaboration.
Strong executive presence and the ability to represent OLYD credibly with external audiences.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
Self-direction, resourcefulness, follow-through, and comfort in a growing organization where every system may not already exist.
Experience building or significantly scaling a philanthropic development function, including creating prospect pipelines, processes, systems, relationships, and operating practices where significant infrastructure was needed.

Preferred

Experience with organizations serving children, youth, families, foster care, education, mentorship, or related social-impact areas.
Experience engaging founders, executives, boards, and volunteer leaders in donor cultivation and solicitation.
Experience developing corporate philanthropy or strategic philanthropic partnerships.
Experience establishing development systems, metrics, and reporting practices.

What Success Looks Like

Success will be reflected in consistent fundraising activity, a growing and qualified donor pipeline, grants and proposals moving forward, stronger philanthropic relationships, increased funding, and a development function that knows what it is doing next and why.

It will also mean building a disciplined, scalable development engine with qualified prospects, strong donor relationships, repeatable processes, effective systems, and a program positioned to grow alongside OLYD.

The CDO will help OLYD build a deliberate, relationship-driven development program capable of supporting our mission for the long term.

Equal Opportunity

Oh! Love Ya Dawn is committed to building a team that reflects a wide range of lived experiences, perspectives, and backgrounds. We believe kindness, respect, and inclusion make our work stronger, and we welcome people who want to grow alongside us.

jobs.description:
About Berkeley

At the University of California, Berkeley, we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom and belonging make it a special place for students, faculty and staff.

As a world-leading institution, Berkeley is known for its academic and research excellence, public mission, diverse student body, and commitment to equity and social justice. Since our founding in 1868, we have driven innovation, creating global intellectual, economic and social value.

We are looking for applicants who reflect California's diversity and want to be part of an inclusive, equity-focused community that views education as a matter of social justice. Please consider whether your values align with our Guiding Values and Principles, Principles of Community, and Strategic Plan.

At UC Berkeley, we believe that learning is a fundamental part of working, and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups (staff organizations). Our goal is for everyone on the Berkeley campus to feel supported and equipped to realize their full potential. We actively support this by providing all of our full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours (10 days) of paid time per year to engage in professional development activities. Find out more about how you can grow your career at UC Berkeley.

Departmental Overview

The University of California, Berkeley is a global leader in fundamental science, influential interdisciplinary research, and fostering technological and policy innovation. With a rich history of discovery and a commitment to creating both short-term and long-term societal benefit, UC Berkeley is uniquely positioned to tackle the most pressing challenges of our time, including the climate crisis and sustainability. Under the leadership of the Associate Provost for Energy, Climate, and Environment (AP-ECE), the Office of the AP-ECE will work collaboratively across campus and with external partners to promote research excellence, curricular innovation, community-engaged scholarship, and sustainable campus operations aligned with the university’s broader strategic goals to provide long-term societal benefit. The Office of the AP-ECE is an entrepreneurial experiment for the Berkeley campus to test the boundaries of what is possible to propel transformative energy, climate and environment scholarship as well as curricular innovation within Berkeley’s ecosystem of excellence.

The Chief Development Officer for the Office of Energy, Climate, and Environment is a senior advancement leader who designs, develops, and delivers fundraising programs that support the university’s broader strategic goals to provide long-term societal benefit. This position reports to the Associate Provost for Energy, Climate, and Environment (AP-ECE) and works across disciplines with academic and fundraising leaders to build relationships with new and existing individual prospects and foundations and create solicitation strategies based on donor capacity and interest.

This is an expert fundraising professional in the area of major and principal gifts. The role maintains a portfolio of donors and prospects and may oversee professional staff if funding allows. The position is expected to raise gift dollar amounts as established annually in collaboration with AP-ECE and University Development and Alumni Relations, at a minimum of $5M annually.

Application Review Date

The First Review Date for this job is June 19, 2026.

For the initial consideration period, please submit application materials by July 10, 2026. The position will be open until filled.

Responsibilities

Develop and manage a portfolio of approximately 40-60 prospects with the capacity to give $5 million or greater, and collaborate with colleagues to advance with a particular focus of those who may give $10 million+. Qualify major gift prospects and solicit gifts directly.
Ensure that predetermined fundraising goals are met and raise at least $5M annually through individual and collaborative fundraising once the portfolio is established.
Build effective relationships across and beyond campus.
Serves as an expert development professional in the area of philanthropy and principal gifts, leading strategies that include highly complex gift discussions and interaction with donors capable of making significant contributions to the university.
Lead proactive collaborative efforts to develop effective and coordinated strategies for prospects shared by more than one academic unit; facilitate action plans and monitor implementation of strategies. Create and execute events and activities for cultivation, stewardship, and solicitations to advance gift conversations.
Drive and manage strategic, consistent, personalized engagement with donors, including meaningful interaction with academic leaders, faculty, and lead campus supporters and volunteers.
Prepare and present formal fundraising proposals to major and principal gift donors and prospects; or prepare senior campus leaders to present proposals.
Ensure that proposals are well crafted, drawing on support from in-house communications team and gaining sign-off from relevant academic leaders.
Ensure that gifts are well-stewarded, drawing on campus partners for appropriate, timely, and consistent recognition, and ensure that all appropriate reporting and documentation is undertaken.
Collaborate and partner with the AP-ECE as well as the VCRO, the Rausser College of Natural Resources, College of Engineering, College of Chemistry, the College of Letters & Science, Organized Research Units as well as other stakeholders to ensure forward momentum with this university-wide priority.
Establish annual fundraising goals and priorities and ensure effective strategy, implementation, and reporting of development activities.
Serve as a trusted advisor on prospect strategies and collaborations with faculty.

Required Qualifications

Substantial years (usually 8+) of high-level performance in principal and major gift fundraising.
Expert knowledge of all aspects of fundraising strategies, structuring complex gifts, donor relations, and advancement communications.
Successful track record in building strong professional relationships with major philanthropists, academic leaders, collaborating development professionals, and other key stakeholders (for ex: faculty and staff).
Relevant field experience, project/program management skills, organization, communication and interpersonal skills as well as strong writing skills.
Advanced knowledge of fundraising in a campaign at an organization with relevant content; demonstrated interest and passion for contributing to access and justice relating to energy, climate, and/or environment.
Expert level skills in maintaining confidentiality.
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.

Salary & Benefits

For information on the comprehensive benefits package offered by the University, please visit the University of California's Compensation & Benefits website.

Under California law, the University of California, Berkeley is required to provide a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role and should not offer a salary outside of the range posted in this job announcement. This range takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, analysis of internal equity, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be offered a salary at or near the top of the range for a position. Salary offers are determined based on final candidate qualifications and experience.

The budgeted annual salary range that the University reasonably expects to pay for this position is $182,800 - $235,000. The full salary range for this job classification is $124,700 - $240,900.

How to Apply

This search is being supported by Berkeley Executive Search (BES).

Conviction History Background

This is a designated position requiring fingerprinting and a background check due to the nature of the job responsibilities. Berkeley does hire people with conviction histories and reviews information received in the context of the job responsibilities. The University reserves the right to make employment contingent upon successful completion of the background check.

Mission Grammar School is an urban, college-preparatory Catholic school located in the Mission Hill neighborhood of Boston, Massachusetts. As the city’s oldest continually operating Catholic school, Mission Grammar has served Boston’s underserved communities for over 138 years, providing scholars from 3 months through 6th grade with access to a high-quality, values-based education.
Today, we serve 310 scholars and are supported by a talented, dedicated faculty who empower students to reach their full potential. Through a strategic $30M capital campaign, currently underway, we are expanding our historic campus to meet the growing needs of families across Boston, enhancing enrollment capacity and creating a modern, 21st-century learning environment that honors our rich legacy.

Resolving the escalations others cannot: diagnosing whether the problem is the model, campus execution, or family fit, engaging the family directly, then writing up the precedent for the rest of the network

Partner with the Office Manager to keep the reader board updated with relevant announcements

Create needed flyers, mailings, or letters in relation to the three main fundraisers and admissions

Responsible for management of the donor database, maintaining data accuracy

Update family status in the donor database as information comes available

Process all charitable gifts to the school, including receiving mail, entering gifts (individual gifts and large batches of gifts) in the donor database, generating letters, sharing weekly reports with Administration

Generate monthly gift reports and summary reports for school Administration and business manager

Bachelor's degree with minimum of two years experience in fundraising and/or school development
Understanding and genuine appreciation of children
Desire to work in a racially and economically diverse, faith-centered community
Experience managing volunteers and collaborating closely with school leadership
Excellent oral and written communication skills that include speaking and inspiring donors
Excellent organizational skills
Excellent editing skills
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, Google Suite, and other design and communication platforms
Preferred active Catholic

jobs.description:
You already built something from zero and took it to scale. Now you're looking for your next big bet—one that has both urgency and moral clarity. If you believe the U.S. education system is criminally under-serving gifted kids, and you’re ready to do something about it, keep reading.

gt.school is redefining what school should look like for high-potential students. Our 2 Hour Learning model compresses the academic day into focused, mastery-based sessions—freeing up time for students to pursue real challenges. Now, we’re ready to build out a physical model campus that adds the missing pieces: leadership experiences, peer competition, performance-driven culture, and the kind of community these students have been missing.

You’ll lead the design, validation, and public rollout of this model campus—with the goal of making it the prototype for a nationwide network. You'll also continue to build our virtual GT Anywhere program together with the team we already have in place. That means testing real-world programming, developing parent demand, building a culture that sticks, and crafting the playbooks to scale it all.

We need someone with founder-level energy and credibility. Someone who understands that the best ideas mean nothing without relentless execution. Someone who can turn a sharp point of view into a school parents can’t stop talking about—and students can’t wait to attend.

What You Will Be Doing

Designing and testing scalable programs that extend beyond academics—focusing on leadership, independence, and competition
Building and validating a physical model campus, including staffing models, space design, and operations
Developing parent-facing messaging, market strategies, and growth playbooks to fuel expansion
Defining, documenting, and scaling quality standards and cultural rituals across all future sites
Acting as the public face of the model—driving visibility through media, events, and partnerships

What You Won’t Be Doing

Stepping into a traditional school role with classrooms, teachers, and a full-day schedule
Catering to families who want gifted-lite programs with AP classes and minimal challenge
Managing incremental change within existing institutions—we're not "fixing" schools, we're replacing them
Chasing superficial engagement metrics—we care about hard outcomes and deep learning, not just activity
Building everything remotely—you'll have flexibility, but will spend ~1 week/month in Austin to ground your work in reality

Program Director Key Responsibilities

Design, validate, and scale a high-performance gifted school model—starting with a single prototype campus and expanding to a national network.

Basic Requirements

Built and scaled a high-impact venture from scratch (bonus if it involved physical operations or education). We are talking about at least 1M USD yearly revenue owned by you
Deep, personal understanding of gifted students—whether through family, professional experience, or lived reality
AI First mentality — Inclination to prioritize AI as the default solution for problem-solving, decision-making and work output generation at scale.
Proven ability to articulate a compelling vision and convert skeptics into believers
Based in the U.S., with ability to travel regularly to Austin (minimum 1 week/month)
Eligible to work in the U.S. without visa sponsorship

About GT School

GT School is revolutionizing education with AI, expert coaching, and 50+ years of learning science. They blend cutting-edge tech with data-driven insights to unlock every student's full potential.

They're on a mission to disrupt the broken education system and unleash the true potential of gifted minds. Forget the one-size-fits-all approach that leaves brilliant students bored and disengaged.

This school has tossed the rulebook and created a modern learning environment powered by AI and guided by dedicated mentors. Their personalized approach accelerates learning - 2-6 times faster than traditional classrooms.

GT School students explore their passions, develop critical thinking skills, and learn to innovate.

Because that's where genius lies.

GT School is where gifted minds turn potential into power.

jobs.description:
The Organization: Meritus College

Meritus College is a new kind of not-for-profit online college, built from the ground up to meet the needs of working adults and career-changers who've been overlooked by traditional higher education.

The problem is clear: only 33% of Pell grant recipients complete their degrees at two-year colleges within six years. College has become too rigid, too expensive, and too disconnected from both student realities and career outcomes. Meritus College is different. Our online, asynchronous programs and "workplace as laboratory" approach allow students to learn and apply new skills directly to their jobs, while receiving personalized support from dedicated coaches every step of the way. We focus on real-world skills and stackable credentials in high-demand fields, ensuring graduates are prepared for today's jobs and tomorrow's opportunities. Founded in 2025 with an inaugural Associate of Applied Science in Technology and Innovation degree, Meritus College is building a mainstream pathway to economic mobility—one designed not for the privileged few, but for the talented many who've too often been left behind.

Role Overview

The primary mission of the Director of Operations is to serve as the connective tissue of Meritus College, ensuring priorities, information, and decisions move effectively across functional areas and that teams have the clarity and infrastructure they need. As Meritus College launches and builds in real time, you will connect dots across the College, proactively identify and unblock issues, escalate issues as needed, and serve as a trusted first line of feedback and thought partnership across the organization.

You will also play a critical role in building the systems, operating rhythms, and infrastructure of the College as it grows, often creating the process while simultaneously moving the work forward. This role sits at the intersection of strategy, operations, and culture, requiring exceptional resourcefulness, critical thinking, and stakeholder management skills to move fluidly between seeing the big picture, building what's missing, and driving the details forward.

The Director of Operations will report directly to Melinda Day, Chief Academic Officer, and will work crossfunctionally across Meritus College teams.

Responsibilities

The responsibilities will include, but are not limited to, the following:

Cross-Functional Program Management

Drive alignment and accountability across Functional Leads through regular status meetings, 1:1 connects, and follow-ups. Introduce and standardize practices, tools, and approaches that strengthen both execution and communications.
Maintain a clear view across all College workstreams, connecting priorities, dependencies, decisions, and information across functional areas.
Proactively identify and resolve blockers, working with Functional Leads and escalating issues to leadership when quick decisions or intervention are needed.
Build a strong, supportive culture among Functional Leads, fostering trust, collaboration, shared accountability, and connection across teams.

Surface patterns, risks, opportunities, and organizational needs to leadership based on a close understanding of what is happening across the College.

jobs.description:
Chief Operating Officer

Reports to: CEO / Founder  
Direct Reports: Leads our deal execution, marketing, and operations teams.  
Location: Carmel, IN (in office)  
Type: Full time

About Highpoint

Highpoint Advisors is a sell-side M&A advisory firm for owners of veterinary, dental, and other healthcare practices. We guide owners through one of the biggest decisions of their careers, from understanding what their practice is worth to closing a sale that fits their goals. Our clients trust us because we act like advisors, not vendors, and every part of the firm is built around that relationship.

The Role

Highpoint is growing, and we are hiring our first Chief Operating Officer to run the firm day to day. You will be the CEO's partner and second in command, turning the firm's strategy into an operating plan and making sure every team has what it needs to deliver for clients.

You will oversee deal execution, marketing and communications, and operations, and own the business functions that hold everything together: finance, people, systems, and process. This role frees our founder to focus on vision, key relationships, and growth, so you will need to be comfortable being the person the team comes to first.

What You Will Do

Lead the firm alongside the CEO

Partner with the CEO to set annual goals, priorities, and the operating plan, then own the execution.
Serve as the first point of escalation for day-to-day decisions across the firm.
Give the CEO a clear, regular view of firm performance, pipeline, and risks.

Oversee deal operations

Own the sell-side deal process, making sure our team has what it needs to guide every client from first conversation to closing day.
Partner closely with the Advisors, who report to the CEO, to support their client work with the right people, process, and tools.
Build visibility into the engagement pipeline.
Manage deal team capacity and analyst support so client work stays on schedule.
Standardize the engagement process, documents, and handoffs so every client gets a consistent, high-quality experience.
Hold the team to clear standards for timelines, CRM use, and client communication.

Run the business side

Own budgeting, forecasting, and financial reporting, working with our outside accounting partners.
Lead people operations: hiring, onboarding, performance reviews, compensation planning, and policies.
Own the firm's systems and tools, including CRM, project management, and document management.
Manage vendors, contracts, insurance, and compliance.
Put simple, scalable processes in place so the firm can grow without adding friction.

Connect growth and client experience

Lead the Director of Marketing & Communications and align marketing and lead generation with deal team capacity and firm goals.
Make sure the client experience is consistent from first contact through closing and beyond, including referrals and client events.
Track the full path from lead to signed engagement to closed deal, and use it to guide investment.

Build the team and culture

Coach and develop your direct reports and help them grow their teams.
Plan headcount ahead of growth and lead hiring for new roles.
Protect the culture that makes Highpoint feel like a trusted advisor to clients and a great place to work for the team.

What Success Looks Like

In the first 90 days

Build strong working relationships with the CEO and each team lead.
Learn the engagement process end to end and sit in on client work across stages.
Deliver an assessment of what is working, what is not, and a prioritized plan for the year.

In the first year

A clear operating rhythm, with goals and scorecards for every team.
Reliable pipeline and capacity reporting that the CEO and leadership team use every week.
A documented, consistent engagement process from signing to close.
Core people practices in place: onboarding, reviews, and a hiring plan.
The CEO spending most of his time on strategy, relationships, and growth rather than daily operations. 

What You Bring

A background in financial services is strongly preferred, such as M&A, investment banking, commercial banking, accounting, wealth management, private equity, or another professional financial services firm.
10 or more years of experience in operations or general management, including at least 5 years in a senior leadership role, ideally in financial or professional services.
Experience leading a small or founder-led firm through growth.
A track record of managing leaders, including revenue-producing or client-facing teams.
Strong financial acumen: budgeting, forecasting, and running a business by the numbers.
Comfort building systems and processes from scratch, and the judgment to keep them simple.
Clear, steady communication with team members, clients, and outside partners.

Strong pluses

Hands-on experience with transactions, deal teams, or client advisory work.
Familiarity with veterinary, dental, or other healthcare practices.
Experience with CRM and pipeline management tools.

Who Thrives Here

You like being close to the work. You are as comfortable in a pipeline review as you are in a hiring conversation. You bring structure without adding bureaucracy, and you care about how clients and team members feel as much as the numbers. You are energized by helping a founder-led firm grow without losing what makes it special.

To apply
, send your resume and a short note about why this role interests you to LeAnne Lavender at llavender@hphadvisors.com .

Highpoint Advisors is an equal opportunity employer.

new_jobs.title: Program Director, Center of Innovation
new_jobs.description:
Who We Are

We are Tennis! The USTA (United States Tennis Association) is the national governing body for the sport of tennis and the leader in promoting and developing the sport’s growth on every level in the United States, from local communities to the crown jewel of the professional game, the US Open.

The USTA Foundation Incorporated (USTAF or USTA Foundation) is the social impact arm of the United States Tennis Association Incorporated (USTA), utilizing the powerful combination of tennis and education to enhance the lives of under-resourced youth through its support of the National Junior Tennis & Learning (NJTL) network. For more than 50 years, NJTL has impacted thousands of under-resourced youth across the nation, and today the network features more than 270 chapters that reach more than 233,000,000 young people from under-resourced communities annually.

Why Work for the USTA?

We are a passionate team of staff and volunteers focused on growing the sport of tennis and making it accessible to all. We are committed to removing barriers and creating opportunities for ALL to participate.

About Lulu's Place

Lulu's Place will offer state-of-the-art facilities in Los Angeles, north of LAX airport, between the communities of Westchester and Playa del Rey, bringing together academic, athletic, and wellness programs for youth from all backgrounds. Trusted partners, including TGR Foundation, a Tiger Woods charity; the United States Tennis Association (USTA) and its charitable arm, USTA Foundation; Cedars-Sinai; and Providence will bring together professional teachers, coaches, mentors, and service providers to deliver high-quality programs to children and their families.

The vision for this project is rooted in the passion and generosity of Carol "Lulu" Kimmelman, a Southern California native, former elementary school teacher in South Los Angeles, and lifelong tennis player who passed away in 2017 after a courageous battle with ovarian cancer. Today, her husband, Doug Kimmelman, and their four children honor Lulu's legacy by advancing her mission to transform young people's lives and create greater equity in sports and education through this groundbreaking youth center.

The Role

The Program Director at Lulu’s Place will lead a youth development program focused on college and career readiness and non-degree career pathways, operating within a shared facility alongside several partner organizations. This position involves a managerial component, overseeing program staff and volunteers.

Operational Oversight: Manage day-to-day operations for USTAF Center of Innovation (CoI), ensuring all activities align with the foundation’s mission, goals, priorities, and safety standards.
Partner Integration: Lead coordination efforts with Lulu's Place Leadership, TGR Foundation, and other on-site program partners to successfully align on shared goals and execution of educational and tennis programming.
Program Development: Lead design and oversee the planning and implementation for direct day, weekend, and afterschool programming. The programs will incorporate the core principles of the NJTL network, tennis, education, and mentorship
Community Engagement: Sets the strategy and is responsible for the USTAF CoI engagement with local community partners, including greater LA NJTL organizations, school districts, charter schools, youth development organizations, and other key community stakeholders.
Quality Assurance: Responsible for the oversight and delivery of USTAF programs and partnered programs to accomplish established and shared goals.
Strategic Growth: Identify opportunities to test and expand programs/products to increase the reach and enhance the impact of NJTL sports-based interventions within the community.

Partner & Facility Coordination

Stakeholder Liaison: Serve as the primary point of contact for diverse community partners, including non-profits, schools, and local NJTL organizations.
Facility Scheduling: Work with the Lulu’s Place facility team and partners to manage the complex master calendars for shared facility use, balancing USTAF programming needs with Lulu's Place partners and community access.
Collaborative Governance: Represent the USTAF by attending all regular partner meetings to ensure effective, efficient communication, align priorities, and minimize confusion and conflicts.
Resource Allocation: Responsible for the USTAF offices and footprint at Lulu's Place.

Impact Measurement & Reporting

Data Collection: Implement systems to track participant attendance, demographic data, and youth development outcomes across all partner programs.
Align with the USTAF leadership in the development of the “measures of success” and align with Lulu's Place partners to align on shared goals

Reporting: Capture and deliver program data into reports for foundation leadership, donors, and community stakeholders.
Evaluation: Use qualitative and quantitative feedback to assess the effectiveness of the "collective impact" model at the facility site.

Compliance & Administration

Safety & Risk Management: Ensure all partners and staff meet Safe Play compliance per the USTA requirements, including regular training and background checks. Ideally, all USTAF staff and program partners will be CPR/First Aid certified, including AED.
Budget Oversight: Manage the USTAF operational budget in collaboration with the leadership of the Programs and Services team of the USTA Foundation.
Grant Compliance: Assist partners in meeting the reporting requirements and performance benchmarks tied to USTA Foundation Program activities and funding
Ensure the program's compliance with all applicable Lulu’s Place youth safety policies, background check requirements, and licensing standards
Establish and oversee data collection, record-keeping, and reporting systems for student participation and outcomes across all program functions
Oversee vendor and service provider relationships (transportation, curriculum materials, technology, etc.)
In addition to the stated compliance and administration duties, review and maintain organizational policies and procedures, updating as needed to reflect best practices and legal requirements
Manage three full-time direct reports

Who You Are

Education: A bachelor’s degree in a related field such as Sports Management, Recreation Administration, Education, Social Work, or Non-Profit Management is required.
Work Experience: 5 to 7 years of experience in program coordination, youth development, or sports administration. Tennis background and/or understanding of the tennis environment is preferred.
Partner Management: Proven track record of managing relationships with community partners, schools, or diverse local organizations is required.
Safety Certifications: Valid CPR, First Aid, and AED certifications (or the ability to obtain them within 30 days of hire) are required.
Clearance: Ability to pass comprehensive, recurring federal and state background checks to work with minors is required.
Technical Proficiency: Strong skills in Microsoft Office Suite (especially Excel), Google Workspace, and familiarity with project management or participant tracking software are required.
Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation for travel between facility sites is required.
Schedule Flexibility: Ability to work non-traditional hours, including evenings and weekends, to align with youth sports schedules is required.
Physical Stamina: Ability to be mobile and active on sports courts or fields for extended periods and lift/move equipment up to 50 lbs is required.

What We Offer

At the USTA, we know people are our most important asset. For this reason, we offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to meet the needs of a diverse workforce!

Flexibility: Our Hybrid with Flexibility approach combines a balance of remote working with in-office collaboration to spark teamwork and creativity.
Comprehensive benefits designed to meet your unique needs: Medical, dental, vision, access to doctors virtually, a flexible spending account to manage your health and dependent care expenses, and life and disability insurance are a small part of our offerings.
Time to recharge and energize: Generous paid time off policy - including vacation, sick, personal, and paid holidays, parental leave, and a paid winter recess.
Plan for your future financially and professionally: 401(k) with employer matching (up to 6.5%), promotional and growth opportunities, Learning and Development programs to learn on the job, and up to $7,000 for tuition reimbursement.
Mental and emotional wellness: Resources for overall well-being, including mental health and meditation benefits.
Other cool perks: A personalized health management program, pet insurance, commuter benefits, identity theft protection, discounts with our network of partners, and fun events are just a few of the optional benefits available.

The expected range for the annual base salary for this position is $85,000 - 105,000.
This role is eligible for an Incentive Compensation Plan (ICP) bonus up to 10%. This range does not include any additional pay or benefits for which a person may qualify. The actual base salary offered is determined by several variables, including, as appropriate, the applicant's qualifications for the position, the years of relevant experience, their unique skills, and the location from which they will be performing the job.

Come One, Come All

We strongly encourage you to apply if you’re interested; we'd love to learn how you can “serve” our team with your unique experience!

USTA is dedicated to providing equal employment opportunities for all individuals, regardless of age, disability, national origin, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, or expression, pregnancy, veteran status, marital status, family status, alienage or citizenship status, creed, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

new_jobs.description:
This position is only open to Sonoma State University Employees

Application Process

This position is open until filled. For full consideration, please submit application, along with cover letter and resume, by 8am on Wednesday, October 21st.

Please review the positio n description listed above for full scope of responsibilities and qualifications.

Job Summary

Reporting to the Director of Equity and Access Programs, the Project Rebound Program Director provides management and guidance in support of the recruitment and success of formerly incarcerated students transitioning into higher education and supervises staff and student personnel. The incumbent supports a broad range of projects involving the development, planning, assessment and execution of programmatic and operational needs, including budget oversight and operational efficiency and effectiveness. The incumbent serves as a strategic partner and liaison with campus and community resources, advocating for program participants and managing the coordination of wraparound student support services. The incumbent ensures compliance with university and program policies, coordinates student services for academic and career success, and assists in the management of program operations and personnel.

Key Qualifications

This position requires three years of progressively responsible professional experience in educational or student support services, with at least one year of experience in program management or coordination, including 1 year of progressively responsible and applicable management and/or supervisory experience. Bachelor’s degree in education, counseling, social work, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred. Must possess demonstrated ability to support and advocate for underrepresented and underserved populations, particularly formerly incarcerated individuals. Experience building partnerships with community organizations and stakeholders highly preferred. Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and Google Workspace; familiarity with PeopleSoft and EAB Navigate preferred.

Salary And Benefits

Starting salary placement depends on qualifications and experience and is anticipated to be in th e range of $6,000- $6,250 a month. This position is a member of the Management Personnel Plan and serves at the pleasure of the President. This position is eligible for a broad range of benefits, including medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurances, retirement (CalPERS), tuition waiver, vacation and sick leave. In addition, 15 paid holidays are offered each year and a Personal Holiday that may be taken any time during the year. Sonoma State University is also a Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program (PSLF) Employer ( comprehensive benefits summary PDF ).

Supplemental Information

About Sonoma State University

Sonoma State University is committed to achieving excellence through teaching, scholarship, learning and inclusion. In line with our Strategic Plan and our Seawolf Commitment, our values include diversity, sustainability, community engagement, respect, responsibility, excellence and integrity. We strive to cultivate a community in which a diverse population can learn and work in an atmosphere of civility and respect. We encourage innovation, experimentation and creativity, as well as contributions to equity and inclusion, in the pursuit of excellence for all members of our university community.

Equal Opportunity & Mandated Reporting

The University is an Affirmative Action/Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, ancestry, age, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, genetic information, medical condition, disability, marital status, or protected veteran status. Mandated Reporting: This position may be considered a "mandated reporter" under the California Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act and is required to comply with the requirements set forth in CSU Executive Order 1083 as a condition of employment.

Employment Eligibility & Conditions

CSU Out of State Policy - Sonoma State University, as part of the CSU system, is a State of California Employer. As such, the University requires all employees upon date of hire to reside in the State of California. As of January 1, 2022 the CSU Out-of-State Employment Policy prohibits the hiring of employees to perform CSU-related work outside the state of California. A background check (including a criminal records check) must be completed satisfactorily before any candidate can be offered a position. Failure to satisfactorily complete the background check may affect the application status of applicants or continued employment of current employees who apply for this position.

Education Code 89521 - Applicants will be required to disclose whether they have received a final administrative decision or final judicial decision determining that they have committed sexual harassment within the last 7 years only after a determination is made that they meet the minimum qualifications for the position, and before an offer of employment is extended. Applicants who reach the final stages of the application process must also sign a release form that authorizes the release of information by the applicant’s current and/or former employers to the CSU concerning any substantiated allegations of misconduct.

Sonoma State University is not a sponsoring agency for staff positions (i.e. H-1B visas).

Positions are posted for a minimum of 14 calendar days.

Application Process & Accommodations

For questions related to the application process, please reach out to hr@sonoma.edu . The ADA Coordinator is also available ( hraccommodations@sonoma.edu ) to assist individuals with disabilities in need of accommodation during the hiring process.

Annual Reports & Safety Information

Sonoma State University's Annual Security Report (https://clery.sonoma.edu/annual-security-report) includes summaries of institutional policy relating to campus safety, drug and alcohol use, sexual assault, and other matters. The report is published in compliance with the Clery Act and includes three years of certain crime statistics that occurred in Clery Act defined geography. A paper copy of the report may be requested in person by emailing the Clery Compliance and Safety Office at clery@sonoma.edu .

Pursuant to the Higher Education Opportunity Act, the Annual Fire Safety Report (AFSR) is available for viewing at https://housing.sonoma.edu/compliance-data/2024-campus-housing-fire-safety-report . The purpose of this report is to disclose statistics for fires that occurred within Sonoma State University student housing facilities for three years, and to distribute fire safety policies and procedures intended to promote safety on campus. A paper copy of the AFSR is available upon request by contacting the Residential Education and Campus Housing at housing@sonoma.edu .

new_jobs.title: Assistant Director of Development, Corporate & Foundation Relations
new_jobs.description:
Join the vibrant community at California State University, Long Beach (CSULB)!

Located just three miles from the Pacific Ocean, CSULB offers an inspiring workplace and an exceptional Southern California lifestyle. Our 322-acre campus—one of the largest in the CSU system—serves more than 42,000 students and is known for its commitment to student success, innovation, and impactful academic and research initiatives.

As a member of the CSULB community, you’ll experience a dynamic environment filled with cultural landmarks, collaborative energy, and opportunities to make a meaningful difference.

Work-life balance thrives here. Long Beach blends coastal relaxation with urban vibrancy, offering miles of beaches, year-round sunshine, a thriving arts and food scene, and convenient access to both Los Angeles and Orange County. It’s an ideal place to grow your career while enjoying everything Southern California has to offer.

Join the California State University (CSU) and explore career opportunities that advance student success and strengthen California’s future—offering competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and professional growth.

Job Summary

The Assistant Director of Corporate & Foundation Relations develops and manages a portfolio of corporate and private foundation prospects and partners to secure philanthropic support for university priorities. The position collaborates with university leadership, faculty, and staff to identify funding opportunities, develop competitive proposals, cultivate and steward relationships, and advance strategic fundraising initiatives that support the university’s mission.

Key Responsibilities

Build and independently manage a portfolio of corporate and foundation prospects, driving all phases of the development life cycle: identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and renewal, with responsibility for securing annual renewals and new entry- and mid-level philanthropic investments in support of university priorities.
Collaborate with faculty and campus partners to research, write, coordinate, and submit grant applications, proposals, and letters of inquiry, with a focus on entry- and mid-level awards ranging from $10,000 to $75,000. Lead the proposal development process with grant seekers and ensure alignment with university policies, approval requirements, and gift and grant compliance standards.
Lead prospect cultivation and stewardship activities, including campus visits, in-person and virtual meetings, presentation materials for corporate and foundation representatives, and the development of impact reports. Create and maintain the CFR LinkedIn page to promote external philanthropic engagement, and produce the CFR Grant Opportunities Digest to increase campus awareness of philanthropic opportunities and application deadlines.

Department

University Development

Time Base

1.0 time-base, 40 hours per week.

Duration of Appointment

This is a temporary position for one year with no permanent status granted. Temporary assignments may expire prior to the ending date.

Classification

Advancement Professional II

Compensation

Salary placement is determined by the education, experience, and qualifications the candidate brings to the position, internal equity, and the hiring department’s fiscal resources.

Hiring Range: The hiring range for this position is $5,274 (Step #1) - $6,303(Step #10) per month commensurate with candidate's education, experience, skills, and training.
CSU Classification Salary Range: The CSU Classification Salary Range for this position is $5,274 (Step #1) - $7,684 (Step #20) per month.

Benefits

At California State University (CSU), we prioritize the health, growth, and success of our employees. Our benefits program reflects our commitment to your overall well-being.

To Be Eligible For Full Benefits, Employees Must Be Appointed At Least Half-time (.50 FTE) With An Appointment Lasting More Than Six Months And One Day. Benefits Eligibility And Offerings May Vary Based On Appointment Type, Classification, And Applicable Collective Bargaining Agreement. Eligible Employees May Have Access To a Comprehensive Benefits Package That Can Include:

Paid Time Off: Up to 24 vacation days per year (based on employee group and/or length of service), 14 paid holidays, and 12 sick days annually with unlimited accrual.
Health Coverage: A variety of medical, dental, and vision plans.
Retirement Plans: Participation in the CalPERS defined benefit plan, along with voluntary savings options such as 403(b), 401(k), and 457 plans.
Educational Benefits: Tuition fee waiver programs for eligible employees; dependent eligibility varies by employee group and bargaining unit.
Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.
Additional Benefits: Wellness programs, professional development opportunities, and insurance options including life, disability, and pet insurance.

Candidates are encouraged to review the appropriate CSU Employee Benefits Summary for details specific to their position. Additionally, the CSU Total Compensation Calculator is available to help prospective employees understand the full value of the CSU benefits package and how it complements base salary.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Strong organizational skills and meticulous attention to detail. Handles tasks with grace and committed to providing quality customer service. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Strong and consistent work ethic and professionalism complimented by a positive attitude and a commitment to diversity, openness, flexibility and integrity. Ability to solicit donations both verbally and in writing via email and/or letter. Ability to travel locally to meet with prospective donors. Ability to establish and maintain good working relationships with a variety of people - volunteers, prospects, donors, faculty, staff, students, and vendors. Ability to be discrete in handling confidential information.

Ability to perform clerical work involving sound judgment, accuracy and efficiency. Establish and maintain collaborative working relationships with program staff, academic departments, the Vice President’s office, and a variety of offices and individuals on and off campus. Working knowledge of Windows, Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams, Zoom, Power Point, Google Docs, Adobe Acrobat, Canva, CRM databases, grant research databases, and social media platforms like LinkedIn.` Ability to communicate with an ethnically and culturally diverse campus community. Ability to follow all university policies, procedures, and guidelines including but not limited to safety, civility, information security, and non-discrimination policies and procedures. Ability to contribute to a positive university experience for each and every student and assist in achieving the university's commitment to a "vision of excellence."

Education And Experience

Equivalent to a bachelor's degree in a related field and two years of related experience required.
Experience in higher education preferred.
The incumbent will be required to travel off campus and be able to travel some distance to accommodate potential donors and must be able to work a flexible schedule, including evenings and weekends.

Licenses

Valid California driver's license required

Application Procedures

Click “Apply Now” to complete the CSULB Online Employment Application.

Please fill out the application completely. It is important that all sections of the online application are completed fully and accurately. Be sure to include all relevant education and experience. Your application will be used to determine whether you meet the minimum qualifications for this position.

Physical Summary

Sedentary work
- Involves mainly sitting. Walking and standing are minimal. Lifting is limited to lightweight objects (10 pounds or less).

Additional Information

CSULB is not a sponsoring agency for staff and management positions (i.e. H-1B Visas).

A background check (including a criminal records check) must be completed satisfactorily and is required for employment. CSULB will make a conditional offer of employment, which may be rescinded if the background check reveals disqualifying information, and/or it is discovered that the candidate knowingly withheld or falsified information. Failure to satisfactorily complete the background check may affect the continued employment of a current CSU employee who was conditionally offered the position.

Equal Employment Statement

Consistent with California law and federal civil rights laws, CSULB provides equal opportunity in employment without unlawful discrimination or preferential treatment based on race, sex, color, ethnicity, national origin, or other protected status. CSULB complies with Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972, the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, the California Equity in Higher Education Act, California’s Proposition 209 (Art. I, Section 31 of the California Constitution), other applicable state and federal anti-discrimination laws, and CSU’s Nondiscrimination Policy. We prohibit discriminatory preferential treatment, segregation based on race or any other protected status, and all forms of discrimination, harassment, and retaliation in all university programs, policies, and practices.

California State University Long Beach expects respectful, professional behavior from its employees in all situations. Acts of harassment or abusive conduct are prohibited. Demonstrated appropriate professional behavior, treating others with civility and respect, and refusing to tolerate abusive conduct is expected of all employees.

Accommodations

We provide reasonable accommodations to applicants and employees with disabilities. Applicants with questions about access or requiring a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application or hiring process should contact StaffHR-Accommodations@csulb.edu .

Out of State Employment Policy

California State University, Long Beach, as part of the CSU system, is a State of California Employer. As such, the University requires all employees upon date of hire to reside in the State of California.

As of January 1, 2022 the CSU Out-of-State Employment Policy prohibits the hiring of employees to perform CSU-related work outside the state of California.

new_jobs.title: Director of Community Engagement, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
new_jobs.description:
"Alpha School students, on average, experience 2.4 to 2.6 times the academic growth of traditional school students"

— Forbes

Alpha is hiring.

Families often come to Alpha through recommendations from people they trust. You will lead the regional relationships that support this growth, connect families and create opportunities for students.

You will design and host gatherings, from eight-person dinners to 150-person open houses; develop a network of parent ambassadors; and build relationships with public officials and business leaders. Through Alpha Networks, you will arrange introductions, expert masterclasses and internships, and welcome graduating families into the alumni community.

You will develop, document and improve the region’s working methods while delivering its programs, sharing effective practices with colleagues in other cities. Success will be measured by the share of enrollment growth generated through personal referrals over several years. The number of introductions and opportunities created per family must also increase as enrollment grows.

No degree or prescribed career path is required. Relevant experience may come from consulting, wealth management, community work, hospitality or advancement. What matters is a record of bringing people together and producing tangible results through those relationships.

The role is on site in Miami, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Boston, Dallas or New York City. It requires regular local travel and hosting commitments on weekday evenings and weekends.

What You Will Be Doing

As Director of Community Engagement, plan and deliver several gatherings each month, including open events, dinners organized by city and grade, and family retreats, within budget.
Secure venues, hosts and vendors, and personally host events.
Recruit current parents as ambassadors, help them share their experiences, and match them with prospective families, including those attending school tours.
Build relationships with public officials and business executives to secure venues, support for new campus openings and opportunities for students.
Connect enrolled families with parent circles and students with mentors, masterclasses and practical internships. Welcome graduating families into the alumni community within 30 days of graduation.
Record every gathering and introduction, and how each family first heard about Alpha, in the customer relationship management (CRM) system. Maintain accurate records of the introductions and opportunities created for each family.

What You Won’t Be Doing

Manage paid advertising or work to targets for impressions or lead volume.
Lead brand communications or central marketing campaigns; these are Marketing’s responsibility.
Process admissions, conduct tours or manage enrollment paperwork; these are the responsibilities of Admissions and Family Success.
Run daily campus operations or manage the opening of physical premises.
Treat attendance figures alone as evidence of success.

Families often come to Alpha through recommendations from people they trust. You will lead the regional relationships that support this growth, connect families and create opportunities for students.

You will develop, document and improve the region’s working methods while delivering its programs, sharing effective practices with colleagues in other cities. Success will be measured by the share of enrollment growth generated through personal referrals over several years. The number of introductions and opportunities created per family must also increase as enrollment grows.

A degree is not required for every candidate, but your background must include at least one of the academic, professional or civic qualifications listed below. You also need a record of bringing people together and producing tangible results through those relationships.

Plan and deliver several gatherings each month, including open events, dinners organized by city and grade, and family retreats, within budget.
Secure venues, hosts and vendors, and personally host events.
Recruit current parents as ambassadors, help them share their experiences, and match them with prospective families, including those attending school tours.
Build relationships with public officials and business executives to secure venues, support for new campus openings and opportunities for students.
Connect enrolled families with parent circles and students with mentors, masterclasses and practical internships. Welcome graduating families into the alumni community within 30 days of graduation.
Record every gathering and introduction, and how each family first heard about Alpha, in the customer relationship management (CRM) system. Maintain accurate records of the introductions and opportunities created for each family.

Manage paid advertising or work to targets for impressions or lead volume.
Lead brand communications or central marketing campaigns; these are Marketing’s responsibility.
Process admissions, conduct tours or manage enrollment paperwork; these are the responsibilities of Admissions and Family Success.
Run daily campus operations or manage the opening of physical premises.
Treat attendance figures alone as evidence of success.
Rely on a completed operating manual, templates or support staff to begin work.

Make personal referrals the source of the majority of enrollment growth in your region.
